entries.name: com.1password.1password
entries.title: 1Password 8
entries.description: Use this section to define settings for 1Password password manager version 8

keys.description: Start at Login -- Force 1Password 8 to start at login
Default Sign-in Address -- Set the default sign-in address for the 1Password app. Users will be prompted to sign in to this account by default.
Enforce Default Sign-in Address -- When enabled, users cannot change the sign-in address from the default value set in authentication.defaultDomain.
Check for compromised websites
Check for two-factor authentication
Check for passkeys
Allow 1Password to prevent your device from sleeping -- Prevents device from sleeping while 1Password is active
Always show Wi-Fi QR codes
Allow connecting to a custom browser
Submit automatically with Universal Autofill -- You can fill your usernames and passwords everywhere you need to sign in on your Mac
Set the password requirement timeframe
Allow Biometric Unlock (Face ID & Touch ID) -- If present enforces whether biometric unlock is allowed (Preferences > Security > Unlock).
Allow Apple Watch Unlock -- If present enforces whether Apple Watch unlock is allowed (Preferences > Security > Unlock).
Allow revealing passwords -- Enforces showing passwords and full credit card numbers (Preferences > Security > Conceal Fields).
Lock on sleep, screensaver, or switching users -- Enforces the configured locked on sleep,screensaver, or switching users (Preferences > Security > Auto-lock).
Lock when main window is closed -- Enforces the configured lock on app exit preference
Set auto-lock timeout -- Enforces the lock on idle time preference (Preferences > Security > Lock).
Clear clipboard after timeout -- The amount of time after copying a 1Password item that it is cleared from the clipboard (Preferences > Security > Clipboard).
Allow Universal Clipboard -- Enforces whether the clear clipboard preference is enabled or disabled (Preferences > Security > Clear clipboard contents).
Show app and website icons -- Show app and website icons
Check for vulnerable passwords -- Check for vulnerable passwords
Automatically check for updates -- Automatically check for updates
Set release channel -- Set release channel

entries.name: com.agilebits.onepassword7
entries.title: 1Password 7
entries.description: Use this section to define settings for 1Password password manager version 7

keys.description: Allow Biometric Unlock (Face ID & Touch ID) -- If present enforces whether biometric unlock is allowed (Preferences > Security > Unlock using ...).
Allow PIN unlock -- If present enforces whether PIN unlock is allowed.
Allow Apple Watch Unlock -- If present enforces whether Apple Watch unlock is allowed (Preferences > Security > Unlock using ...).

Master Password Timeout -- Enforces a configured master password timeout (Preferences > Security > Require Master Password every ...) if: 1) Biometric or Apple Watch unlock is possible based on the related preferences and the hardware configuration 2) The user has configured…
Conceal Passwords -- Enforces the configured conceal passwords setting (Preferences > Security > Conceal Passwords).
Lock on Sleep -- Enforces the configured lock on sleep setting (Preferences > Security > Lock on sleep).
Lock on Screen Saver -- Enforces the configured lock on screen saver setting (Preferences > Security > Lock when screen saver is activated).
Lock on App Exit -- Enforces the configured lock on app exit preference (Preferences > Security > Lock when main window is closed).
Lock on User Switch -- Enforces the configured lock on user switch preference (Preferences > Security > Lock when fast user switching).
Lock on Idle -- Enforces whether the lock on idle preference is enabled or disabled (Preferences > Security > Lock after computer is idle).
Lock on Idle Time -- Enforces the lock on idle time preference (Preferences > Security > Lock after computer is idle).
Clear Clipboard -- Enforces whether the clear clipboard preference is enabled or disabled (Preferences > Security > Clear clipboard contents).
Clear Clipboard Time -- Enforces the clear clipboard contents after X seconds preference (Preferences > Security > Clipboard)
Check for Compromised Websites (Watchtower) Notification -- If enabled, creates a user notification when Watchtower detects a compromised website.
Vault Access Added/Removed Notification -- If enabled, creates a user notification when vault access is added or removed.
One-Time Password Copied to Clipboard Notification -- If enabled, creates a user notification when a vault item's OTP code is copied to the clipboard.
What's New Prompt -- If enabled, on app launch following an update a What's New dialog box is presented to the user.
Check for Software Updates -- Enforces whether to automatically check for available updates.
Automatically Install Software Updates -- Should 1Password attempt to automatically install updates?
Install Or Update -- The software titles to automatically install or update (even if they are not currently installed) using the Patch Agent.
Update Only -- The software titles to automatically update if installed and out-of-date using the Patch Agent.
Other Managed Software -- The software titles to enable the Active Intervals feature for even when not included in the InstallOrUpdate or UpdateOnly preference keys.

Run Interval -- The Patch Agent runs every 4 hours by default. You can adjust this interval time for your environment. Note: This key is configured in seconds. The minimum setting is 600 seconds (10 minutes) and there is currently no maximum.

Skip First Patch Agent Run -- When Alectrona Patch runs for the first time, it performs what is called a "Patch Agent Run" where it runs all configured installs/updates. You can skip the first Patch Agent Run by setting this key to true.

Active Intervals -- The Patch Agent will attempt to silently update any recently deferred app that exists in the InstallOrUpdate or UpdateOnly keys immediately after that app has been terminated by the user (even during an interval period).

Remove Patch Symlink -- Set to true to remove the symlink located at /usr/local/bin/patch. This will remove patch from the user's $PATH and allows for accessing the built-in BSD patch command (opens new window)without using it's full path.
Recon After Installs -- Set to true to perform a Jamf Pro inventory update after a software title is installed or updated using the Patch Agent.
Defer If Running -- If an app is running when an update occurs, setting this key to true will suppress the update dialog and automatically perform a deferral.
Update Mac App Store apps -- Set to true to attempt to update and convert Mac App Store (MAS) apps to their non-MAS counterpart.
Dialog Description -- The main description that appears in the update dialog.
Update Button Label -- The label or displayed text in the update button.
Defer Button Label -- The label or displayed text in the defer button.
Update Button Primary -- By default, the Update button is the primary button of the Update Dialog; meaning it responds to the Return key. Set this key to false if you wish to disable this behavior.
Content Image Path -- Path to a locally stored image to use as the content image of the update dialog (PNG/JPG/GIF/TIFF).
Dialog Timeout -- The duration, in seconds, that the update dialog will appear on screen before performing a timeout.
Dialog Help Text -- Enable the help button and populate the text displayed on screen when clicked.
Dialog Help Tool Tip -- Customizes the tooltip of the help button (when enabled).
Dialog Title -- The title of the update dialog window.
Deferral Limit -- Sets a global Deferral Limit for all software.
Deferral Limit Exceptions -- Sets exceptions to the global Deferral Limit, or irrespective of it.

subkeys.description: Key -- Software ID of the software title to include in the deferral limit exceptions.
Integer -- Deferral limit for the specified Software ID.

keys.description: Final Dialog Description -- The main description that appears in the final update dialog.
Dialog Deferral Text -- The text that appears below the main description in the update dialog.
Ignore Deferral Text -- Does not include the deferral text in the update dialog’s description.
Record Timeout as Deferral -- When an update dialog timeout occurs, record a deferral rather than taking no action.
Final Dialog Timeout -- The duration, in seconds, that the final update dialog will appear on screen before performing an update.

entries.name: com.alectrona.patch
entries.title: Alectrona Patch Command Line Tool
entries.description: Alectrona Patch Command Line Tool settings

keys.description: License Key -- Your license key provided upon subscription to Alectrona Patch.

Force Login Organization UUID(s) -- Require login to belong to a specific organization. Accepts a single UUID string, which also pre-selects that organization during login, or an array of UUIDs where any listed organization is accepted without pre-selection.

subkeys.description: Organization UUID

keys.description: Disable Auto Updates -- Disable automatic updates for Claude Desktop.
Auto Update Enforcement Hours -- Hours before forcefully restarting Claude to apply a prepared update. Must be between 1 and 72 hours.
Check for updates on releases.claude.com -- Read the update feed from releases.claude.com so api.anthropic.com can stay blocked. Defaults to false.

Configuration relaunch window -- Hours a user may keep working on the old configuration after a managed-configuration change is detected. 0 = restart required at once. Blank = 24 hours. Defaults to 24. Range: 0-336.
Configuration re-check interval -- Minutes between the running app's checks for a changed managed configuration. Blank = 10 minutes. Defaults to 10. Range: 2-30.
Enable Desktop Extensions -- Enable or disable Claude Desktop extensions.
Enable Extension Directory -- Enable or disable access to the extension directory.
Enable Local MCP Servers -- Enable or disable local Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.
Enable Claude Code for Desktop -- Enable Claude code access in desktop.
Enable Secure VM Features -- Enable Cowork access in desktop
Allow Cowork -- Enable Cowork. Claude works on longer tasks like research, analysis, and documents. Defaults to true.

Enable Built-in Browser -- Claude Desktop on third-party inference deployments. Enable the built-in browser in Cowork and Code sessions. False disables the browser pane; Code retains its localhost-only dev-server preview. Defaults to false.

Built-in Browser Default Site Policy -- Claude Desktop on third-party inference deployments. Default policy for sites Claude may open, read, or act on when the built-in browser is enabled. Allowed domains are exceptions under block; blocked domains are exceptions under allow.

Built-in Browser Allowed Domains -- Claude Desktop on third-party inference deployments. Sites Claude may open, read, or act on when builtinBrowserDefaultDomainPolicy is block; ignored under allow. Empty or unset allows no external sites for Claude. Users can still view other sites.

subkeys.description: Domain -- A hostname or supported hostname wildcard. A plain hostname also matches its www form, but no other subdomain.

keys.description: Built-in Browser Blocked Domains -- Claude Desktop on third-party inference deployments. Sites Claude may not open, read, or act on when builtinBrowserDefaultDomainPolicy is allow; ignored under block. Empty or unset adds no blocked sites.

subkeys.description: Domain -- A hostname or supported hostname wildcard. A plain hostname also matches its www form, but no other subdomain.

keys.description: Microsoft 365 native sign-in broker -- Set to “disabled” to force browser-based Microsoft 365 sign-in instead of the native Company Portal / Windows account broker. One of: auto, disabled. Defaults to auto.
Require Signed Desktop Extensions -- When true, Claude Desktop rejects extensions that aren't signed by a trusted publisher.

Disabled Built-in Tools -- Removes the listed built-in tools from the available set in Claude Desktop. Known tools: Task, Bash, Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, Skill, REPL, JavaScript, AskUserQuestion.

subkeys.description: Tool -- Name of a built-in tool to disable.

keys.description: Managed MCP Servers -- Distributes remote MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers to users. Each entry requires a unique name and an HTTPS URL. Optional fields include transport, headers, OAuth, and tool-level policies.

subkeys.description: Managed MCP Server
Name -- Unique name identifying this MCP server.
URL -- HTTPS URL of the remote MCP server.
Transport -- Transport protocol used to reach the MCP server.
Headers -- Static request headers used to authenticate to the MCP server (for example, Authorization). Mutually exclusive with the OAuth field.
Header Value
OAuth -- When true, Claude Desktop runs a PKCE OAuth flow at first use to acquire user credentials. Mutually exclusive with the Headers field.
Tool Policy -- Maps tool names exposed by the MCP server to a policy. Allowed values per tool: allow, ask, blocked. The "ask" policy prompts the user to confirm before the tool runs.
Policy

keys.description: Allow persistent tool approvals -- Offer the persistent “Always allow” approval options for MCP tools. Disable to keep tool approvals per-call or session-scoped only. Defaults to true.
MCP tool call timeout -- Per-call timeout for MCP tool calls, in seconds. Default 180 (3 minutes). Range: 60-3600.
Organization UUID -- A UUID you generate. Tags telemetry so Anthropic support can locate your fleet's events, and namespaces each user's local data. Not used for auth.
Block essential telemetry -- Crash and performance reports to Anthropic. Defaults to false.
Block nonessential telemetry -- Product-usage analytics and diagnostic-report uploads. No message content. Defaults to false.
Block nonessential services -- Connector favicons and the artifact-preview and MCP Apps widget iframe origins. Artifacts will not render. Defaults to false.
Effort Level -- Sets the default effort level for Claude Code sessions in Claude Desktop.
Allowed Workspace Folders -- Folders where Claude may work. Applies to both Cowork and Code sessions. Leave unset for unrestricted access.

subkeys.description: Path -- Absolute folder path. May start with ~ or one of the listed %VAR% tokens, expanded per user. Subfolders are included.
Select Default -- Shows as a folder chip on the new-task page and skips the trust prompt. Users can remove it.
Mode -- Read-only folders can be viewed and searched but not modified in Cowork. In Code, applies to file tools only; Bash and SSH do not yet enforce read-only. One of: rw, ro.

keys.description: Disable bypass permissions mode -- Remove the bypass permissions mode from Code sessions and Cowork tasks, so Claude always follows the permission policy. Off by default.
Block reads outside working directories -- Keep Claude from reading files outside a Code session's working directories. File tools refuse such reads; sandboxed shell commands lose the home directory.
Disable Claude.ai sign-in -- Users see only this provider at the login screen. The option to sign in to Claude.ai is hidden. Defaults to false.
Disable claude:// deep-link handling -- Stop external apps and websites from opening Claude Desktop via claude:// links. Defaults to false.
Allow Chat -- Enable Chat. Quick questions and drafting.
Advanced file analysis -- Allow Claude to run code in a local sandbox to analyze attached files it can't read natively — like Excel and PowerPoint. Off by default.

Max tokens per window -- Per-user soft cap, counted client-side over the token cap window. Not a server-enforced quota. Requires inferenceTokenWindowHours to also be set — without a window length the cap is inert and no limit is enforced.

Token cap window -- Tumbling window length for the token cap. Max 720 hours (30 days). Range: 1-720. Required when inferenceMaxTokensPerWindow is set — the cap only takes effect once both are configured.
End-user attribution -- Show the signed-in user's identity-provider identity in the sidebar and account menu, and emit it as the OpenTelemetry enduser.id resource attribute.
Deployment display name -- Overrides the provider label shown in the sidebar footer, user-menu header, and connection-error banner.
Deployment display subtitle -- Optional detail shown after the deployment display name in the account-menu header.
Hide configuration deprecation warnings -- Don't show users the in-app warning that this configuration uses a deprecated field. The final reminder in the 24 hours before the cut-off still appears.
Organization banner -- A persistent banner across the top of the app window after sign-in.

subkeys.description: Enabled -- Turns the banner on or off.
Text -- Text shown in the banner.
Background color -- Banner background color, as a hex code.
Text color -- Banner text color, as a hex code.
Link URL -- URL the banner links to when clicked.

keys.description: Hide feature announcements -- Suppress unprompted feature-announcement UI: the post-update “What's new” nudge and new-feature tips. Users can still open release notes themselves. Defaults to false.
Claude.ai data import -- Lets users import Claude.ai chats and projects, plus earlier Claude sessions on this computer, when enabled is true. automatic3pImport is a separate switch.

subkeys.description: Enabled -- Turns history import on. The banner and import actions stay off until this is true.
Export enabled -- Lets users export Claude.ai chats and projects. automatic3pImport is a separate switch.
Banner behavior -- When the import banner appears.

keys.description: OpenTelemetry collector endpoint -- Where OpenTelemetry logs and metrics are sent. Leave blank to disable.
OpenTelemetry exporter protocol -- grpc or http/protobuf. One of: http/protobuf, http/json, grpc. Defaults to http/protobuf.
OpenTelemetry exporter headers -- Static collector headers — routing and tenant headers only. No credentials here; use Collector authentication or the headers helper script for tokens.
Collector authentication -- inference-credential sends the user's inference bearer token to the collector as Authorization: Bearer. One of: none, inference-credential.
OpenTelemetry headers helper script -- Absolute path to an executable that prints a JSON object of collector headers. Merged over the static headers and Collector authentication; the helper wins.
OpenTelemetry resource attributes -- Extra resource attributes to attach to every span/metric. A static enduser.id set here always wins over the runtime identity.

Desktop telemetry export level -- Controls the Claude Desktop application's events, separate from Cowork and Code sessions. Defaults to error. One of: off, error, warn, info, debug. Defaults to error.

Content capture categories -- Content categories the desktop exporter sends unredacted to your collector. Leave empty to redact all content (default). One of: userPrompts, assistantResponses, toolDetails, toolContent, rawApiBodies.

subkeys.description: Content capture category -- Name of a content capture category to enable a class of raw content in OpenTelemetry events sent to your collector (this data never reaches Anthropic)

keys.description: Export traces -- Also export OpenTelemetry traces from Cowork tasks and Code sessions. Uses Claude Code's session tracing.
Whats New displayed -- Suppress the Whats New screen on the selected versions of Compressor.

subkeys.description: Suppressed

keys.description: Active Directory Realm -- The host name of your organization's Active Directory domain.
Run Periodic State Check -- Enable or Disable periodic state checking. Customers who expose their DNS to the public Internet will need to disable periodic state checking.
Organization Username Label -- The name your organization gives usernames.
Pre Populated Username -- Upon launch or sign out, Enterprise Connect will pre-populate the Username field with this username.

Preferred Domain Controller -- Preferred domain controller when doing LDAP queries and getting a Kerberos TGT. If this domain controller is unavailable, Enterprise Connect will fall back to domain controllers it discovers from DNS.
Reminder Nag Interval -- The interval, in seconds, between setup notifications.
Get Renewable TGT -- Acquire a renewable Kerberos TGT.
Show Menu Extra -- Determines whether the Enterprise Connect menu extra is loaded.
Show Legacy Certificates -- Automatically check the "Show Legacy Certificates" option in the certificate chooser window.
Show Keychain Identities -- Automatically check the "Show Legacy Certificates" option in the certificate chooser window.
Organization Logo Path -- The path to a file containing your organization's logo, in PNG, JPG or GIF format.
Debug Mode -- Enables debugging mode.
Sync Local Password -- Enables Active Directory to local account password sync. This only works if the user is logged into their Mac with a local account.
Password Required Complexity -- Tells Enterprise Connect that passwords should meet Active Directory's definition of complexity. Used to enable and configure live password testing.
Password Required Complexity Disable Unicode -- Disables the "Has a Unicode character" password test from live password testing.
Password Required Length -- Require passwords to be at least as long as the specified value.
Password Change Message Path -- Path to a RTF file to display for the user during password changes.
Password History Count -- How many previous passwords cannot be re-used.
Password Minimum Age -- The minimum age of passwords before they can be changed.

Disable Password Functions -- Disable Enterprise Connect's password management abilities, including expiration notices and the "Change Password" menu item. This is useful for customers who don't change their passwords in AD.
Disable Password Expiration Checking -- Disable Enterprise Connect's password expiration checking, but still leave intact the ability for the user to change their password with Enterprise Connect.
Run Password Change Script On Local Password Sync -- Determines if Enterprise Connect should run the password change script upon a local password sync.
Password Change Script Path -- Path to the password change script.
Password Change URL -- URL to open in the user's default web browser when they use Enterprise Connect to change their password. Standard password change functionality will no longer work.
Password Expire Override -- Override domain password policy when calculating password expiration.
Password Expire Notification -- Determines the amount of days before password expiration that the user receives expiration notifications.
Check For Network Server -- Check for a host in your organization's network.
Network Server -- The host Enterprise Connect should check for when connecting.

Connect Delay -- Delay starting the connection process when your organization's network is detected. This may be useful for customers who use Cisco NAC and need to delay connection while host checks are performed.
Connection Completed Script Path -- Path to the connection completed script.
Connection Reminder Interval -- The interval, in seconds, between connection reminders.
Daily Reconnect Time -- The interval, in seconds, that Enterprise Connect should attempt its daily reconnect. Set this to 0 to disable the daily reconnect.
Run Audit Script -- Tells Enterprise Connect to execute an audit script.
Audit Script Path -- Path to the audit script.
Mount Network Home Directory -- Determines if Enterprise Connect mounts the user's network home directory.
Prevent User Shares -- Prevents the user from adding custom shares to Enterprise Connect.
Managed Shares -- List of shares that Enterprise Connect should attempt to mount. Users will still be able to add their own shares.

subkeys.description: Share
Path

keys.description: Share Mount Delay -- Delay the mounting of network shares when your organization's network is detected. This may be useful for customers who use Cisco NAC and need to delay connection while host checks are performed.
Enable Smart Card Mode -- Determines whether smart card mode should be enabled.
Show Username in Smart Card Mode -- Determines if Enterprise Connect should display the username field if smart card mode is enabled.
Destroy Kerberos Ticket on Smart Card Removal
Welcome displayed -- Suppress the Welcome screen on the selected versions of Final Cut Pro.

subkeys.description: Suppressed

keys.description: Whats New displayed -- Suppress the Whats New screen on the selected versions of Final Cut Pro.

subkeys.description: Suppressed

keys.description: Suppress Welcome Screen -- If enabled, suppresses the welcome screen.
Download Additional Content Prompt -- If disabled, suppresses the prompt to download additional optional GarageBand content.

Suppress What's New Prompt -- So long as the integer value of this preference is set equal or higher to the value produced in the user-level plist after launching the app and acknowledging the "What's New" prompt, this will prevent the "What's New" prompt from appearing.
FFiMovieUpgradeFirstRun -- Suppresses the popup to upgrade an iMovie library on first run.
Welcome displayed -- Suppress the Welcome screen on the selected versions of iMovie.

subkeys.description: Suppressed

keys.description: Whats New displayed -- Suppress the Whats New screen on the selected versions of iMovie.

subkeys.description: Suppressed

keys.description: Don't Show Additional Content Download -- Suppresses the popup to download additonal sound content on launch. Yes, in fact, 'Download' is spelled 'Dowload' in the preference key.
Enable Additional Option: Audio -- Enables destructive audio editing, and advanced configuration options for audio editing experts.
Enable Additional Option: Control Surfaces -- Allows experts to create new, and edit any functional detail of existing control surface systems.
Enable Additional Option: Advanced Editing -- Enables advanced editing functionality, including: aliases, track reassignment, historic tuning scales, and the Tempo Interpreter.
Enable Additional Option: MIDI -- Allows signal flow control and real-time processing of MIDI input and output streams in the Environment.
Enable Additional Option: Score -- Enables the full feature set of the Score window for notation experts.
Enable Additional Option: Surround -- Enables all features for surround audio productions, and requires a surround speaker setup for monitoring.
Enable Show Advanced Tools -- Configures whether Show Advanced Tools is enabled.

allowedValueTitles: Create New Project Using Default Template
keys.description: Startup Action -- Configures Logic's startup behaviour.

Suppress What's New Prompt -- So long as the integer value of this preference is set equal or higher to the value produced in the user-level plist after launching the app and acknowledging the "What's New" prompt, this will prevent the "What's New" prompt from appearing.
Quick Help Mode -- Set to 0 to disable Quick Help Mode overlays.
Upgrade Checked -- Suppresses the popup to upgrade an Motion on first run.
Whats New displayed -- Suppress the Whats New screen on the selected versions of Motion.

subkeys.description: Suppressed

keys.description: Set this preference to 'false' to forcibly disable adding the ".txt" extension to plain text files.
Set this preference to 'false' to forcibly disable grammar checking with spelling.
Set this preference to 'false' to forcibly disable spell checking while typing.
Set this preference to 'false' to forcibly disable automatic spelling correction.

Set this preference to 'true' to forcibly enable data detectors. Data detectors can automatically detect date, time, and contact information, which can then be used to update a contact, create a new Calendar event, and more.
By default, the Window Size height is 30 lines. Enable this setting to change this default window height.
Set this preference to 'true' to display .html files as HTML code instead of formatted text when opening a file.
Set this preference to 'true' to display .rtf files as RTF code instead of formatted text when opening a file.
Set this preference to 'false' to suppress TextEdit messages when closing documents saved on storage volumes that don't support Apple's permanent version storage.
Plain Text Font -- Enter the name of the desired plain text font. This defaults to Menlo. String format: Find your desired font file in either /System/Library/Fonts or /Library/Fonts.
Plain Text Font Size -- Enter the desired font size for plain text documents.
Rich Text Font -- Enter the name of the desired rich text font. This defaults to Helvetica. String format: Find your desired font file in either /System/Library/Fonts or /Library/Fonts.
Rich Text Font Size -- Enter the desired font size for rich text documents.
Set this preference to 'false' to not include code that preserves the white space in your document's formatted text.
Set this preference to 'true' to forcibly make text wrap to document margins, rather than window boundaries.
Set this preference to 'false' to not show the ruler in rich text documents by default.
Set this preference to 'false' to forcibly disable "smart" copy/paste.
Set this preference to 'false' to forcibly disable "smart" links.
Set this preference to 'false' to forcibly disable "smart" quotes.
Set this preference to 'true' to enable "smart" substitutions for quotes and dashes in rich text documents. Takes effect for newly opened documents and after "Make Plain Text".
Set this preference to 'false' to forcibly disable text replacement.
Set this preference to choose a specific encoding method for opening plain text files, rather than "Automatic".
Set this preference to choose a specific encoding method for saving plain text files, rather than "Automatic".
Text Default File Format -- Enable this preference to forcibly apply a default TextEdit file format. By default, TextEdit defaults to rich text - .rtf -, rather than plain text - .txt

Enable this setting for HTML Embedded CSS styling. ex. UseEmbeddedCSS = true == "Embedded CSS" ex. UseEmbeddedCSS = true & UseInlineCSS = false == "Embedded CSS" ex. UseEmbeddedCSS = false & UseInlineCSS = false == "No CSS"

Enable this setting for HTML Inline CSS styling. ex. UseInlineCSS = true == "Inline CSS" ex. UseInlineCSS = true & UseEmbeddedCSS = false == "Inline CSS" ex. UseInlineCSS = false & UseEmbeddedCSS = false == "No CSS"
Set this preference to 'false' to use the "Strict" HTML or XHTML document type, rather than "Transitional". ex. UseTransiontalDocType = false & UseXHTMLDocType = false == "HTML Strict" ex.

Set this preference to 'false' to use the HTML, rather than the XHTML document type. ex. UseTransiontalDocType = false & UseXHTMLDocType = false == "HTML Strict" ex. UseTransiontalDocType = false & UseXHTMLDocType = true == "XHTML Strict" ex.
By default, the Window Size width is 90 lines. Enable this setting to change this default window width.
Default Document Author -- Enter a default author name for documents.
Default Document Organization / Company -- Enter a default organization / company for documents.
Default Document Copyright -- Enter a default copyright for documents.
Application Appearance -- Offers you three choices to control BBEdit’s appearance.
Editor color scheme -- Allows you to easily select any existing color scheme.
Editor color scheme (dark mode) -- Allows you to easily select any existing color scheme.

Status bar item size -- Controls whether the text and icons displayed in the navigation bar, the status bar, and in the sidebars of editing, project, and differences windows are of normal, large, or extra-large size.
List display font size -- Controls the size of the system font used to display text in browser list panes, including disk browsers, search results browsers, FTP/SFTP browsers, etc.
Application icon -- Allows you to control which icon BBEdit presents in the Finder (if possible) and in the Dock (while the application is running).
Navigation bar items: Text options -- Displays the Text Options popover in the navigation bar.
Navigation bar items: Document navigation -- Displays the Document popup menu in the navigation bar.
Navigation bar items: Marker menu -- Displays the Marker popup menu in the navigation bar.
Navigation bar items: File versions -- Displays the File Revisions button in the navigation bar.
Navigation bar items: Related files -- Displays the Related Files button in the navigation bar.
Navigation bar items: Document status -- Displays the document status icon in the navigation bar.
Navigation bar items: Function menu -- Displays the Function popup menu in the navigation bar.
Navigation bar items: Sort items by name -- Displays the Function popup menu in the navigation bar.
Editing window: Line numbers -- Displays line numbers along the left edge of the window.
Editing window: Gutter -- Displays the gutter.
Editing window: Tab stops -- Displays tab stops as vertical grid lines within the content area of text windows, using the tab width set in the Editor Defaults panel.
Editing window: Page guide at -- Displays the page guide.
Editing window: Page guide at ## characters -- Displays the page guide at the specified character width.
Editing window: Guide contrast -- Adjusts the contrast level of the page guide display region.
Text status bar items: Cursor position -- Displays the current location (line and column) of the insertion point, or the endpoint of the current selection range in the status bar.
Text status bar items: Language -- Displays the Language popup menu in the status bar.
Text status bar items: Text encoding -- Displays the Text Encoding popup menu in the status bar.
Text status bar items: Line break type -- Displays the Line Break Type popup menu in the status bar.
Text status bar items: Document lock state -- Displays a padlock icon in the status bar to represent the document’s current lock state.
Text status bar items: Document save date -- Displays the current document’s last saved date and time (if applicable) in the status bar.
Text status bar items: Document statistics -- Displays an item in the status bar which shows the number of characters, words, and lines in the document.
Text status bar items: Instances of selected text -- Displays either the number of matches for the selected text within the document, or the word surrounding the insertion point if applicable.
Text status bar items: Text magnification -- Displays the Magnification popup in the status bar.

Open documents into the front window when possible -- Controls whether BBEdit should attempt to open newly created or opened documents into the frontmost window (if possible), or whether each document should open directly into a separate text window.
Automatically refresh documents as they change on disk -- Checks if documents have changed on disk while they’re open.
Remember the ## most recently used items -- How many files appear on the Open Recent sub-menu
Always show full paths in "Open Recent" menu -- Always display full paths in the Open Recent menu.
When BBEdit becomes active -- Controls what BBEdit does when you launch it, or activate it when there are no open windows.

Reopen documents that were open at last quit -- Remember what documents (as well as disk browsers and FTP/SFTP browsers) were open when you choose the “Quit” command, and will attempt to reopen those documents the next time you launch it.
Restore unsaved changes -- Will preserve the contents of any unsaved document contents when you quit and restore those documents the next time you launch it.
Include documents on FTP/SFTP servers -- Attempt to reopen documents from remote servers when you launch BBEdit.
Always fetch fron server -- Always reconnect and reload all files previously opened from remote servers.
Automatically check for updates -- Automatically looks to see if a newer version is available.
Early Access -- Checks for pre-release versions.
Default model -- The default model BBEdit should use for ChatGPT.
Wrap lines in responses -- Responses should be wrapped.
Wrap lines in responses to ## characters -- Set the character width at which lines within responses should be wrapped.
Show text completions -- Choose when BBEdit will display text completions.
Delay XX seconds before automatic completion -- Choose when BBEdit will display text completions.
Include dictionary words in completion list -- Will include dictionary words in the text completion list.

Include system text replacements in completion list -- Will include any system-wide Text Replacement triggers (as configured in the “Keyboard” system preferences) which begin with the text you typed in the completion popup.
Insert matching delimiters while typing -- Typing any opening delimiter will cause BBEdit to immediately insert the appropriate closing delimiter.
Suround selected text when typing matching delimiters -- Typing an opening delimiter will cause BBEdit to surround the selected text with a matched pair of delimiters.
Display instances of selected text -- Will display all occurrences of the selection within the current document.
Underline or Highlight -- Will display all occurrences of the selection within the current document via either underlining or highlighting.
Delay XX seconds -- Adjust the duration of the delay before BBEdit applies highlighting.
Show tick marks in scroll bars: Instances of selected text -- Shows tick marks for instances of selected text.
Show tick marks in scroll bars: Live Search results -- Shows tick marks for instances of Live Search results.
Show tick marks in scroll bars: Spelling errors -- Shows tick marks for instances of spelling errors.
Show tick marks in scroll bars: Issues -- Shows tick marks for instances of issues.
Show issues -- Will display LSP-generated diagnostics when available.
Highlight insertion point -- Will highlight the line that currently contains the insertion point.

Use "hard" lines in soft-wrapped views -- The line number bar, position display, and Line Number commands in editing views will use line and character position numbers that correspond to the “hard” line breaks actually present in the document, rather than the soft-wrapped line breaks.
Insertion point -- Choose your desired insertion point cursor style.
Line spacing -- Adjust the amount of space between lines of text in editing views.
Extra vertical space ("overscroll") in text views -- Allows you to specify how much empty space BBEdit should leave after the end of each document’s content.
Allow pinch-to-zoom to change magnification -- Use touchpad pinch gestures to increase or decrease the magnification level of the frontmost (active) document.
Enable single-click line selection -- Select lines by single-clicking on them in the line number bar or gutter.
Cut/Copy entire line for insertion point -- The Cut and Copy commands will act upon the entire line which contains the insertion point, in order to make life easier for Windows refugees.
When opening a document: Collapse folds -- Will automatically collapse all folds.
When opening a document: Collapse folds below level # -- Specifies the level to collaps folds.
Invisibles display: tabs -- Allows you to specify alternative characters for tabs.
Invisibles display: line breaks -- Allows you to specify alternative characters for tabs.
Default font -- Controls the standard font and font size which BBEdit uses to display the contents of text windows. This is in "data" format.
Override document setting -- Will cause the default font to always prevail over any previously saved font settings associated with a given text file.
Spaces per tab -- Controls the default number of spaces that BBEdit uses to represent the width of a tab character.
Magnification -- Sets the default magnification for new text documents.
Auto-indent -- Pressing the Return key in new windows automatically inserts spaces or tabs to indent the new line to the same level as the previous line.
Balance while typing -- Flashes the matching open parenthesis, brace, bracket, or curly quote when you type a closing one.
Use typographer's quotes -- Will automatically substitutes curly (or typographer’s) quotes (“ ” ‘ ’) for straight quotes (" ') in any new documents you create.
Auto-expand tabs -- Inserts an appropriate number of spaces instead of a tab character every time you press the Tab key.
Show invisible characters -- Shows or hides non-printing characters in the window.
Show spaces -- Will display placeholder characters for spaces.
Show tabs -- Will display placeholder characters for tabs.
Show line breaks -- Will display placeholder characters for line breaks.
Check spelling as you type -- Will automatically check spelling as you type, and underline any potentially misspelled words.
Soft wrap text to -- Soft-wraps the text in the file to the right margin that you choose.
Soft wrap text to: Page guide/Windows width/Character width -- Soft-wraps the text in the file to the right margin that you choose.
Soft wrap text to: Character width -- Soft-wraps the text in the file to the right margin that you choose.
Soft-wrapped line indentation -- Lets you specify how BBEdit should indent soft wrapped text.
Use Tab key to navigate Placeholders -- Will jump to the next placeholder in the document (if any) when you press the Tab key, or the previous placeholder if you press Shift-Tab.

allowedValueTitles: Scroll to begining and end of document
Move cursor to begining and end of current line
keys.description: "Home" and "End" key behavior -- This setting will have the Home and End keys perform these respective actions.
Enter key generates Return -- Will generate a line break when you press the Enter key.
Allow Tab key to indent text blocks -- You can press the Tab key to invoke the Shift Right command, or Shift-Tab to invoke the Shift Left command.
Enable Shift-Delete for forward delete -- Holding down the Shift key with the Delete key makes the Delete key work the same way as the Forward Delete key on extended keyboards.
Enable macOS "Help" key -- Pressing the Insert key present on some PC-style keyboards will open BBEdit’s Help book.

When auto-indenting, remove leading white space from indented line -- When you type Return, BBEdit will insert a line break and strip the following whitespace, leaving the remaining text also left-aligned.

Allow Page Up and Page Down keys to move the insertion point -- Move the insertion point to the same relative position within the window in each new screenful of text displayed by Page Up or Page Down.
Option-↑ and option-↓ move by paragraphs -- The Option-Up arrow and Option-Down arrow key shortcuts will advance to the previous or next paragraph.
Emulate Emacs key bindings -- This option allows you to use the basic Emacs navigation keystrokes to move around in editing views.
Display status window -- Will display a small palette which shows Emacs shortcuts as you type them.

Enable meta sequences -- Will intercept presses of the Escape key and use these to emulate a meta key to generate Emacs command sequences, at the cost of no longer being able to use the Escape key to exit full screen mode.
Allow the Escape key to trigger text completion -- Pressing the Escape key will trigger text completion.
Default Language for New Documents -- If you like, you can set the default language for new untitled documents.
Default Language for Unmapped files -- If you like, you can set the default language for unmapped documents.

Custom filesname extension mappings -- You may add (or remove) additional extension mapping via the Custom Extension Mappings list. The values for the keys Language: Code and Language: Name need to match.

keys.description: Markdown processor -- Allows you to select which built-in, or installed and recognized, Markdown processor BBEdit should employ to convert Markdown content to HTML for previewing and export. BBEdit has built-in support for ‘cmark’ as well as ‘classic’ Markdown.
Custom command line: Command -- The command name must be available in your $PATH.
Custom command line: Arguments -- The command arguments must be separated by spaces.
Printing font -- specifies the default font BBEdit uses for printing when the “Print using document’s font” option is turned off.
Custom printing font -- Uses the specified font and tab settings when printing. This is in "data" format.
Frame printing area -- Draws a box along the edges of the printed text.
Print page headers -- Prints the page number, the name of the file, the time and date printed in a header at the top of each page.
Print full path -- Prints the full path of the file being printed in the header.
Print line numbers -- Prints line numbers along the left edge of the paper.
1-inch gutter -- Leaves a one-inch margin along the left edge of the paper.
Print color syntax -- Prints all colorized text within the document in color.
Time stamp -- Choose whether the date that appears in the printed page header is the date that the file was last modified or the date that the file was printed.

allowedValueTitles: Only if the printed document is wrapped for display
keys.description: Wrap Text to Printed Page -- Choose whether a document’s contents should always be soft-wrapped upon printing, or only if soft wrapping is enabled for that document.

Automatically show sidebar: AlwaysShowFileList -- Controls whether BBEdit should display the sidebar only as needed. The preference setting in BBEdit actually controlls two keys; AlwaysShowFileList and AutoShowFileList.

Automatically show sidebar: AutoShowFileList -- Controls whether BBEdit should display the sidebar only as needed. The preference setting in BBEdit actually controlls two keys; AlwaysShowFileList and AutoShowFileList.
Reshape window when showing or hiding sidebar -- Will reshape the entire window when the sidebar appears (or is hidden) to maintain the editing pane at a consistent size.
Add documents to sidebar in alphabetical order -- Will add newly created and/or opened documents to the sidebar list in alphabetical order.
Sidebar list appearance and behavior: Show icons -- Displays icons for files and folders in the sidebar’s file list.
Sidebar list appearance and behavior: Show Finder tags -- Displays the Finder tags for files and folders in the sidebar’s file list.

Sidebar list appearance and behavior: Allow keyboard focus -- The sidebar lists in projects, multi-document editing windows, and differences windows can acquire keyboard focus (by clicking or tabbing into them), and you can then use conventional keyboard navigation gestures to change the selection.

Background -- Controls the background color used within editing windows. This needs to be entered as a comma seperated list of hue, saturation, lightness, and alpha (transparency). Example: hsla(0.668, 0.001, 0.970, 1.000)

Misspelled words -- Controls the color BBEdit uses to highlight misspelled words. This needs to be entered as a comma seperated list of hue, saturation, lightness, and alpha (transparency). Example: hsla(1.001, 0.503, 1.000, 1.000)

Spaces -- Controls the color BBEdit uses to display spaces when the Show Invisibles and Show Spaces display options are active. This needs to be entered as a comma seperated list of hue, saturation, lightness, and alpha (transparency).

Other invisibles -- Controls the color BBEdit uses to display invisible characters other than spaces when the Show Invisibles display options is active. This needs to be entered as a comma seperated list of hue, saturation, lightness, and alpha (transparency).

Differences -- Controls the color BBEdit uses to highlight differing regions within a Differences window. This needs to be entered as a comma seperated list of hue, saturation, lightness, and alpha (transparency). Example: hsla(0.759, 0.311, 1.000, 1.000)
Sub-line differences -- Provides explicit control over the color BBEdit uses to display character ranges within a single top-level (or line-level) difference, rather than using a derived color.

Insertion point line -- Controls the color BBEdit uses to highlight the current line the insertion point is located at. This needs to be entered as a comma seperated list of hue, saturation, lightness, and alpha (transparency). Example: hsla(0.172, 0.116, 0.976, 1.000)

Use custom highlight colors: primary -- Choose the primary highlight color. This needs to be entered as a comma seperated list of hue, saturation, lightness, and alpha (transparency). Example: hsla(0.591, 0.298, 1.000, 1.000)

Use custom highlight colors: primary -- Choose the secondary highlight color. This needs to be entered as a comma seperated list of hue, saturation, lightness, and alpha (transparency). Example: hsla(0.668, 0.001, 0.864, 1.000)
Text Encodings -- Allows you to choose which of these encodings BBEdit includes in its menus.
Default text encoding for new documents -- Uses the encoding specified by this option for new documents which do not contain an intrinsic encoding specification.

If a file's encoding can't be guessed, try -- If BBEdit cannot determine a file’s proper encoding by examination, it will try opening the file using the encodings contained in this list, in the order they appear. The default required value is "Western (Mac OS Roman)".

Line breaks -- If BBEdit cannot determine a file’s proper encoding by examination, it will try opening the file using the encodings contained in this list, in the order they appear. The default required value is "Western (Mac OS Roman)".
Ensure file ends with line break -- Will add a line break at the end of the file if there is not already one present.
Strip trailing whitespaces -- Will trim all trailing non-vertical whitespace from the document file before writing it out.
Make backup before saving -- Automatically make a backup copy of each file that you save.
Keep historical backups -- Will preserve backups in the “BBEdit Backups” folder.
Preserve file name extension -- Have BBEdit place the tilde after the “base” name of the file (“foo~.html”) instead of the name of the original with a tilde appended (“foo.html~”).

Rescue untitled document contents when discarding changes -- When this option is on and you close an untitled document (one that has never been saved to disk), and click “Don't Save”, BBEdit will preserve a snapshot of that document's contents.
Remove rescued items -- Will automatically perform some housekeeping for you by cleaning up rescued data.
Remove rescued items after ## days -- You can adjust the interval from 1 to 365 days.
Text file name extensions -- Add filename extensions for files that BBEdit does not intrinsically know about, but which should be treated as (plain) text files.

Prompt To Reopen Remote Documents -- If set to 'false', BBEdit will not attempt to open any documents that were opened from FTP/SFTP servers. Defaults to 'true'. If set to 'false', BBEdit will open remote documents without asking, if ReopenRemoteDocuments is set to 'true'.

Ask XCode to Open File by Name -- If Xcode is running, Open Selection and Open File by Name will ask it for a path to the file name; if something useful comes back, BBEdit will open it.

BRIEF State Timeout -- The progressive (BRIEF compatible) behavior of the Home and End keys operates within a specific time period; if you wait longer than that, the behavior state resets. The factory default timeout period is ten seconds.

Camel Case Navigation Includes Underscores -- When using "camel case" navigation (see above), BBEdit does not include underscores ( _ ) when moving or extending the selection range. If you would prefer that it do so, you can turn this on.

Color Patterns In Grep Cheat Sheet -- BBEdit will color patterns (the left-hand column) in the Grep Cheat Sheet menu according to the active color scheme. If you would prefer monochromatic patterns for any reason turn this off.

Editor: Auto Word Count Size Threshold -- Automatic word counting is disabled for documents over a set size threshold, in order to avoid needless delays when working on very large documents. The factory default is 16M characters - 16777216 -, but you may change this limit.

Editor: Control Arrow Camel Case -- BBEdit supports "camel case" navigation: press Control-left-arrow or Control-right-arrow to jump to the next (or previous) transition from lower-case to upper-case characters (or a word boundary, whichever comes first).

Editor: Control Arrow H Scroll -- BBEdit supports "camel case" navigation: press Control-left-arrow or Control-right-arrow to jump to the next (or previous) transition from lower-case to upper-case characters (or a word boundary, whichever comes first).

Editor: Delete Indentation Whitespace To Tab Stop -- When you backspace from the insertion point, BBEdit will delete a tab stop's worth of spaces if there are only spaces (and tabs) between the insertion point and the start of the line on which you're editing.

Editor: Soft Wrap Length Threshold -- For text documents whose size exceeds a certain threshold (expressed in bytes), BBEdit will ignore the Soft Wrap Text preference and leave wrapping off in order to improve the performance of opening very large files.

Editor: Spell Check Length Limit -- Since "Find All Misspelled Words" is pretty much pointless on files over a certain size, the maximum amount of text checked by this command is limited to 1M - 1024 squared - characters. This may be adjusted.

Fixed Width Font Smoothing Threshold -- Whether or not BBEdit uses text smoothing - antialiasing - may be adjusted separately for fixed-width and for proportional fonts. The factory default smoothing thresholds are 8pt for fixed width fonts, and 4pt for proportional fonts, respectively.

Surf Next Previous In Display Order -- When using the "Previous Document" and "Next Document" commands on the View menu, or the navigation arrows in the navigation bar, the order in which BBEdit navigates documents is determined by the order in which they were opened.

Use Separators In Unix Script Output -- Ordinarily, the output from Unix scripts run within BBEdit is delimited with line separators - except when the script output is sent to a new untitled document. If you wish to suppress the separators, you can set this to 'false'.
Use System Font For Line Bar -- BBEdit uses the document's display font to draw line numbers in the line number bar. This may be less than ideal if the display font isn't monospaced.
Use Tab Key As Completion Trigger -- To use the Tab key to trigger text completion, set this preference to 'true'.

Use XML Markup Rules For HTML5 -- Ordinarily, BBEdit will generate XHTML-style markup in HTML5 documents (those with a "<!DOCTYPE HTML>" declaration). If you wish, you can suppress this by setting this to 'false'.

allowedValueTitles: Always: Always write the HFS file type and creator (the pre-8.6 behavior)
Never: Never set the HFS file type and creator (even if the document’s volume supports it)
Smart: Write HFS file type and creator only if the document’s volume supports it
keys.description: Write Extended Attributes -- By default, BBEdit will avoid writing extended attributes - HFS Type/Creator - to volumes which don't natively support them - i.e. to avoid creating the ._FILE - when it is safe to do so. We'll be able to re-open the document correctly later.

Zoom Windows In Place -- BBEdit attempts to move windows as little as possible when you zoom them. To override this and let BBEdit place the window in the upper left-hand corner of the screen, set this to 'false'.

Automatic Update Install Prompt -- Controls the automatic update install prompt. When enabled, presents users with the option to allow automatic download and install of available updates. If disabled, disallows automatic updates and requires manual installation every time.
Enable Automatic Silent Updates -- Controls automatic silent updates. If enabled, users will not be informed about updates and updates will be silently installed when the app quits.
Enable Automatic Update Checks -- Controls automatic update checks.

Sparkle Feed URL -- Setting this to a non-existent URL will disable the ability for users to manually check for updates. Useful when you intend to use your own software distribution mechanism to deploy updates.
Automatic Update Check Interval -- Controls the automatic update check interval. The default is 1 day (86400 seconds). Setting to 0 disables updates.

Enable Cloud Reporting -- Enables Brave Browser cloud reporting. When this policy is left unset or set to False, there is no data collected or uploaded. When this policy is set to True, the data is collected and uploaded to Google Admin console.

Enable Cloud Extension Install Requests -- Enables Brave Browser extension installation requests. When the policy CloudReportingEnabled is left unset or set to disabled, this policy will be ignored, extension installation requests are not created or uploaded.
Report Safe Browsing -- Report Safe Browsing information.

allowedValueTitles: Do not allow any site to use the clipboard site permission
Allow sites to ask the user to grant the clipboard site permission
keys.description: Default clipboard setting -- This policy only affects clipboard operations controlled by the clipboard site permission, and does not affect sanitized clipboard writes or trusted copy and paste operations.

allowedValueTitles: Allow all sites to set local data
Do not allow any site to set local data
Keep cookies for the duration of the session
keys.description: Default cookies setting -- Allows you to set whether websites are allowed to set local data. Setting local data can be either allowed for all websites or denied for all websites.
Block third party cookies -- Enabling this setting prevents cookies from being set by web page elements that are not from the domain that is in the browser's address bar.
Allow cookies on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are allowed to set cookies.
Block cookies on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are not allowed to set cookies.
Limit cookies from matching URLs to the current session -- Cookies set by pages matching these URL patterns will be limited to the current session, i.e. they will be deleted when the browser exits.

allowedValueTitles: Do not allow any site to request access to Bluetooth devices via the Web Bluetooth API
Allow sites to ask the user to grant access to a nearby Bluetooth device
keys.description: Control use of the Web Bluetooth API -- Allows you to set whether websites are allowed to get access to nearby Bluetooth devices. Access can be completely blocked, or the user can be asked every time a website wants to get access to nearby Bluetooth devices.

allowedValueTitles: Do not allow any site to request access to USB devices via the WebUSB API
Allow sites to ask the user to grant access to a connected USB device
keys.description: Control use of the WebUSB API -- Allows you to set whether websites are allowed to get access to connected USB devices. Access can be completely blocked, or the user can be asked every time a website wants to get access to connected USB devices.

allowedValueTitles: Allow all sites to show all images
Do not allow any site to show images
keys.description: Default images setting -- Allows you to set whether websites are allowed to display images. Displaying images can be either allowed for all websites or denied for all websites.
Allow images on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are allowed to display images.
Block images on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are not allowed to display images.

allowedValueTitles: Do not allow any site to load mixed content
Allow users to add exceptions to allow mixed content
keys.description: Default insecure content setting -- Control use of insecure content exceptions. Allows you to set whether users can add exceptions to allow mixed content for specific sites.

Allow insecure content on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are allowed to display blockable (i.e. active) mixed content (i.e. HTTP content on HTTPS sites) and for which optionally blockable mixed content upgrades will be disabled.

Block insecure content on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are not allowed to display blockable (i.e. active) mixed content (i.e. HTTP content on HTTPS sites), and for which optionally blockable (i.e. passive) mixed content will be upgraded.

allowedValueTitles: Allow all sites to run JavaScript
Do not allow any site to run JavaScript
keys.description: Default JavaScript setting -- Allows you to set whether websites are allowed to run JavaScript. Running JavaScript can be either allowed for all websites or denied for all websites.
Allow JavaScript on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are allowed to run JavaScript.
Block JavaScript on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are not allowed to run JavaScript.

allowedValueTitles: Revert to legacy SameSite behavior for cookies on all sites
Use SameSite-by-default behavior for cookies on all sites
keys.description: Enable legacy SameSite cookie behavior -- Allows you to revert all cookies to legacy SameSite behavior.
Enable legacy SameSite cookie behavior for list of domains -- Cookies set for domains matching these patterns will revert to legacy SameSite behavior.

allowedValueTitles: Allow all sites to automatically run the Flash plugin
keys.description: Default Flash setting -- Allows you to set whether websites are allowed to automatically run the Flash plugin. Automatically running the Flash plugin can be either allowed for all websites or denied for all websites.
Allow the Flash plugin on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are allowed to run the Flash plugin.

allowedValueTitles: Allow sites to show desktop notifications
Do not allow any site to show desktop notifications
Ask every time a site wants to show desktop notifications
keys.description: Default notification setting -- Allows you to set whether websites are allowed to display desktop notifications. Displaying desktop notifications can be allowed by default, denied by default or the user can be asked every time a website wants to show desktop notifications.
Allow notifications on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are allowed to display notifications.
Block notifications on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are not allowed to display notifications.
Allow local file access to file:// URLs on these sites in the PDF Viewer -- Setting this policy allows the domains listed to access file:// URLs in the PDF Viewer.
Block the Flash plugin on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are not allowed to run the Flash plugin.

allowedValueTitles: Allow all sites to show pop-ups
Do not allow any site to show popups
keys.description: Default popups setting -- Allows you to set whether websites are allowed to show pop-ups. Showing popups can be either allowed for all websites or denied for all websites.

allowedValueTitles: Allow third-party storage partitioning to be enabled
Block third-party storage partitioning from being enabled
keys.description: Default Third Party Storage Partitioning Setting -- Third-party storage partitioning is on by default for some users as of M113, but can be disabled via Brave Browser flag. If this policy is set to AllowPartitioning or unset, third-party storage partitioning may be enabled.
Allow popups on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are allowed to open popups.
Block popups on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are not allowed to open popups.

Automatically select client certificates for these sites -- Allows you to specify a list of url patterns that specify sites for which Brave Browser should automatically select a client certificate, if the site requests a certificate.

allowedValueTitles: Allow sites to track the users' physical location
Do not allow any site to track the users' physical location
Ask whenever a site wants to track the users' physical location
keys.description: Default geolocation setting -- Allows you to set whether websites are allowed to track the users' physical location. Tracking the users' physical location can be allowed by default, denied by default or the user can be asked every time a website requests the physical location.

allowedValueTitles: Do not allow any site to access the camera and microphone
Ask every time a site wants to access the camera and/or microphone
keys.description: Default mediastream setting -- Allows you to set whether websites are allowed to get access to media capture devices.
Register protocol handlers -- Allows you to register a list of protocol handlers. This can only be a recommended policy.

Third Party Storage Partitioning Blocked For Origins -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify top-level (the url in the tab's address bar) origins which block third-party storage partitioning (partitioning of cross-origin iframe storage).

Automatically grant permission to these sites to connect to USB devices with the given vendor and product IDs -- Allows you to set a list of urls that specify which sites will automatically be granted permission to access a USB device with the given vendor and product IDs.
Allow media autoplay -- Allows you to control if videos can play automatically (without user consent) with audio content in Brave Browser.
Allow media autoplay on a whitelist of URL patterns -- Controls the whitelist of URL patterns that autoplay will always be enabled on.
Allow media autoplay on an allow list of URL patterns -- Controls the allow list of URL patterns that autoplay will always be enabled on.

List of alternate URLs for the default search provider -- Specifies a list of alternate URLs that can be used to extract search terms from the search engine. The URLs should contain the string '{searchTerms}', which will be used to extract the search terms.
Enable the default search provider -- Enables the use of a default search provider.

Default search provider encodings -- Specifies the character encodings supported by the search provider. Encodings are code page names like UTF-8, GB2312, and ISO-8859-1. They are tried in the order provided.
Default search provider icon -- Specifies the favorite icon URL of the default search provider.

Parameter providing search-by-image feature for the default search provider -- Specifies the URL of the search engine used to provide image search. Search requests will be sent using the GET method. If the DefaultSearchProviderImageURLPostParams policy is set then image search requests will use the POST method instead.

Parameters for image URL which uses POST -- Specifies the parameters used when doing image search with POST. It consists of comma-separated name/value pairs. If a value is a template parameter, like {imageThumbnail} in above example, it will be replaced with real image thumbnail data.
Default search provider keyword -- Specifies the keyword, which is the shortcut used in the omnibox to trigger the search for this provider.
Default search provider name -- Specifies the name of the default search provider. If left empty or not set, the host name specified by the search URL will be used.
Default search provider new tab page URL -- Specifies the URL that a search engine uses to provide a new tab page.

Default search provider search URL -- Specifies the URL of the search engine used when doing a default search. The URL should contain the string '{searchTerms}', which will be replaced at query time by the terms the user is searching for.

Parameters for search URL which uses POST -- Specifies the parameters used when searching a URL with POST. It consists of comma-separated name/value pairs. If a value is a template parameter, like {searchTerms} in above example, it will be replaced with real search terms data.

Default search provider suggest URL -- Specifies the URL of the search engine used to provide search suggestions. The URL should contain the string '{searchTerms}', which will be replaced at query time by the text the user has entered so far.

Parameters for suggest URL which uses POST -- Specifies the parameters used when doing suggestion search with POST. It consists of comma-separated name/value pairs. If a value is a template parameter, like {searchTerms} in above example, it will be replaced with real search terms data.
Types of extensions/apps that are allowed to be installed -- Controls which app/extension types are allowed to be installed and limits runtime access.
URL patterns to allow extension, app, and user script installs from -- Allows you to specify which URLs are allowed to install extensions, apps, and themes.
Extension ID Blacklist -- Allows you to specify which extensions the users can NOT install. Extensions already installed will be disabled if denied, without a way for the user to enable them.
Extension ID Blocklist -- Allows you to specify which extensions the users can NOT install. Extensions already installed will be disabled if denied, without a way for the user to enable them.
Extension ID Whitelist -- Allows you to specify which extensions are not subject to the blacklist.
Extension ID Allowlist -- Allows you to specify which extensions are not subject to the blocklist.

allowedValueTitles: Manifest v2 is enabled for forced extensions only
keys.description: ExtensionManifestV2Availability -- Control if Manifest v2 extensions can be used by browser.

Extension/App IDs and update URLs to be silently installed -- Specifies a list of apps and extensions that are installed silently, without user interaction, and which cannot be uninstalled nor disabled by the user.
Extension management settings -- Configures extension management settings for Brave Browser. A default configuration can be set for the special ID "*"

Allow insecure extension updates -- Allow insecure algorithms in integrity checks on extension updates and installs.

Enable Google Cast -- If this policy is set to true or is not set, Google Cast will be enabled, and users will be able to launch it from the app menu, page context menus, media controls on Cast-enabled websites, and (if shown) the Cast toolbar icon.
Show the Google Cast toolbar icon -- If this policy is set to true, the Cast toolbar icon will always be shown on the toolbar or the overflow menu, and users will not be able to remove it.
Cross-origin HTTP Basic Auth prompts -- Controls whether third-party sub-content on a page is allowed to pop-up an HTTP Basic Auth dialog box.
Kerberos delegation KDC policy -- Use KDC policy to delegate credentials. Controls whether approval by KDC policy is respected to decide whether to delegate Kerberos tickets.
Kerberos delegation server whitelist -- Servers that Brave Browser may delegate to.
Kerberos delegation server allowlist -- Servers that Brave Browser may delegate to.

Supported authentication schemes -- Specifies which HTTP authentication schemes are supported by Brave Browser. Possible values are 'basic', 'digest', 'ntlm' and 'negotiate'. Separate multiple values with commas.

Authentication server whitelist -- Specifies which servers should be whitelisted for integrated authentication. Integrated authentication is only enabled when Brave Browser receives an authentication challenge from a proxy or from a server which is in this permitted list.

Allow Basic authentication for HTTP -- Setting the policy to Enabled or leaving it unset will allow Basic authentication challenges received over non-secure HTTP. Setting the policy to Disabled forbids non-secure HTTP requests from using the Basic authentication scheme; only secure HTTPS…

Authentication server allowlist -- Specifies which servers should be allowed for integrated authentication. Integrated authentication is only enabled when Brave Browser receives an authentication challenge from a proxy or from a server which is in this permitted list.
Disable CNAME lookup when negotiating Kerberos authentication -- Specifies whether the generated Kerberos SPN is based on the canonical DNS name or the original name entered.
Include non-standard port in Kerberos SPN -- Specifies whether the generated Kerberos SPN should include a non-standard port.
Enable NTLMv2 authentication -- Controls whether NTLMv2 is enabled.
Browser Switcher Enabled -- This policy controls whether to enable Legacy Browser Support. When this policy is set to true, Brave Browser will attempt to launch some URLs in an alternate browser.
Alternative Browser Parameters -- This policy controls command-line parameters to launch to the alternative browser.
Alternative Browser Path -- This policy controls which command to use to open URLs in an alternative browser.

Browser Switcher Delay -- This policy controls how long to wait before launching an alternative browser, in milliseconds. When this policy is set to a number, Brave Browser shows a message for that many milliseconds, and then opens the alternative browser.
Keep Brave Browser open when the last tab switches to another browser -- This policy controls whether to close Brave Browser completely when the last tab would switch to another browser.
Browser Switcher URL List -- This policy controls the list of websites to open in an alternative browser.
Browser Switcher URL Greylist -- This policy controls the list of websites that will never cause a browser switch.

Browser Switcher External Greylist URL -- This policy is a URL, that points to an XML file in the same format as Internet Explorer's SiteList policy. This loads rules from an XML file, without sharing those rules with Internet Explorer.

Browser Switcher External Sitelist URL -- This policy is a URL, that points to an XML file in the same format as Internet Explorer's SiteList policy. This loads rules from an XML file, without sharing those rules with Internet Explorer.
Abusive Experience Intervention Enforce -- Allows you to set whether sites with abusive experiences should be prevented from opening new windows or tabs.
Allow accessibility descriptions for Google images -- Enable Get Image Descriptions from Google. Enables visually-impaired screen reader users to get descriptions of unlabeled images on the web.

allowedValueTitles: Do not allow ads on sites with intrusive ads
keys.description: Ads setting for sites with intrusive ads -- Allows you to set whether ads should be blocked on sites with intrusive ads.
Local Network Access Restrictions Enabled -- A policy to control whether users are prompted to allow sites to ask for Local Network Access.
Local Network Access Allowed For URLs -- A policy to automatically grant specific sites Local Network Access.
Local Network Access Blocked For URLs -- A policy to automatically deny specific sites Local Network Access.
Privacy Sandbox Ad Measurement Enabled -- A policy to control whether the Privacy Sandbox Ad measurement setting can be disabled for your users.
Privacy Sandbox Ad Topics Enabled -- A policy to control whether the Privacy Sandbox Ad measurement setting can be disabled for your users.
Privacy Sandbox Prompt Enabled -- A policy to control whether your users see the Privacy Sandbox prompt.
Privacy Sandbox Site Enabled Ads Enabled -- A policy to control whether the Privacy Sandbox Site-suggested ads setting can be disabled for your users.
Enable Advanced Protection -- Enable additional protections for users enrolled in the Advanced Protection program.
Advanced Protection Deep Scanning -- This policy controls whether users enrolled in the Advanced Protection program are allowed to send their downloads to Google for malware scanning.
Enable deleting browser and download history -- Enables deleting browser history and download history in Brave Browser and prevents users from changing this setting.
Allow Dinosaur Easter Egg Game -- Allow users to play dinosaur easter egg game when device is offline.
Allow invocation of file selection dialogs -- Allows access to local files on the machine by allowing Brave Browser to display file selection dialogs.
Allow running plugins that are outdated -- If you enable this setting, outdated plugins are used as normal plugins.
Allow a page to show popups during its unloading -- This policy allows an admin to specify that a page may show popups during its unloading.
Allows a page to perform synchronous XHR requests during page dismissal. -- This policy allows an admin to specify that a page may send synchronous XHR requests during page dismissal.
Allow web authentication requests on sites with broken TLS certificates -- This policy will allow WebAuthn on sites with invalid TLS certificates.
Define domains allowed to access G Suite -- Enables Brave Browser's restricted log in feature in G Suite and prevents users from changing this setting.
Enable alternate error pages -- Enables the use of alternate error pages that are built into Brave Browser (such as 'page not found') and prevents users from changing this setting.
Always Open PDF files externally -- Disables the internal PDF viewer in Brave Browser. Instead it treats it as download and allows the user to open PDF files with the default application.

allowedValueTitles: Enable in incognito and regular sessions
Enable in guest and regular sessions
Enable in regular, incognito and guest sessions
keys.description: Ambient Authentication -- Configuring this policy will allow/disallow ambient authenticaiton for Incognito and Guest profiles in Brave Browser.
Force Enable App Cache -- Allows the AppCache feature to be re-enabled even if it is off by default.

Allow or deny audio capture -- If enabled or not configured (default), the user will be prompted for audio capture access except for URLs configured in the AudioCaptureAllowedUrls list which will be granted access without prompting.

Enable the audio sandbox -- Allow the audio sandbox to run. If this policy is enabled, the audio process will run sandboxed. If this policy is disabled, the audio process will run unsandboxed and the WebRTC audio-processing module will run in the renderer process.

URLs that will be granted access to audio capture devices without prompt -- Patterns in this list will be matched against the security origin of the requesting URL. If a match is found, access to audio capture devices will be granted without prompt.
Enable AutoFill -- Enable AutoFill. This policy is deprecated in M70, please use AutofillAddressEnabled and AutofillCreditCardEnabled instead.
Allow protocols to auto launch external applications -- Define a list of protocols that can launch an external application from listed origins without prompting the user.
