keys.description: Whether online OCSP/CRL checks are performed -- In light of the fact that soft-fail, online revocation checks provide no effective security benefit, they are disabled by default in Google Chrome version 19 and later.

Enabled Plugins -- This policy is deprecated. Please use the DefaultPluginsSetting to control the avalability of the Flash plugin and AlwaysOpenPdfExternally to control whether the integrated PDF viewer should be used for opening PDF files.
Enable TLS Encrypted ClientHello -- This policy will allow encryption of TLS ClientHello for enhanced privacy.
Enable Managed Extensions to use the Enterprise Hardware API -- When this policy is set to enabled, extensions installed by enterprise policy are allowed to use the Enterprise Hardware Platform API.
Keep browsing data when creating enterprise profile by default -- This policy will allow keeping browsing data in new enterprise profiles

Check Safe Browsing status of URLs in real time -- This policy controls checking URLs in real time to identify unsafe URLs. If this policy is left not set or set to ‘Disabled', the consumer Safe Browsing checks will be applied.
Display "Always open" checkbox in external protocol dialog -- Show an "Always open" checkbox in external protocol dialog.
Allow file or directory picker APIs to be called without prior user gesture -- This policy will allow file picker APIs without user gesture for specified origins

Enable force sign in for Google Chrome -- If this policy is set to true, user has to sign in to Google Chrome with their profile before using the browser. And the default value of BrowserGuestModeEnabled will be set to false.

Force Google SafeSearch -- Forces queries in Google Web Search to be done with SafeSearch set to active and prevents users from changing this setting.

Force SafeSearch -- This policy is deprecated, please use ForceGoogleSafeSearch and ForceYouTubeRestrict instead. This policy is ignored if either the ForceGoogleSafeSearch, the ForceYouTubeRestrict or the (deprecated) ForceYouTubeSafetyMode policies are set.
Force Legacy Default Referrer -- This enterprise policy is for short-term adaptation and will be removed in M82.
Enable globally scoped HTTP auth cache -- This policy configures a single global per profile cache with HTTP server authentication credentials.
Enable Google Search Side Panel -- This policy will allow Google Search Side Panel.

Enforce Strict Restricted Mode for YouTube
keys.description: Force minimum YouTube Restricted Mode -- Enforces a minimum Restricted Mode on YouTube and prevents users from picking a less restricted mode.

Force YouTube Safety Mode -- This policy is deprecated. Consider using ForceYouTubeRestrict, which overrides this policy and allows more fine-grained tuning. Forces YouTube Moderate Restricted Mode and prevents users from changing this setting.
Use hardware acceleration when available -- If this policy is set to true or left unset, hardware acceleration will be enabled unless a certain GPU feature is blacklisted.
Hide the web store from the New Tab Page and app launcher -- Hide the Chrome Web Store app and footer link from the New Tab Page and Google Chrome OS app launcher.

HSTS Policy Bypass List -- List of names that will bypass the HSTS policy check. Hostnames specified in this list will be exempt from the HSTS policy check that could potentially upgrade requests from http to https.

keys.description: Enable HTTP/0.9 support on non-default ports -- This policy enables HTTP/0.9 on ports other than 80 for HTTP and 443 for HTTPS.
Enable automatic HTTPS upgrades -- This policy will allow automatic HTTPS upgrades.

Import autofill form data from default browser on first run -- This policy forces the autofill form data to be imported from the previous default browser if enabled. If enabled, this policy also affects the import dialog.
Import bookmarks from default browser on first run -- This policy forces bookmarks to be imported from the current default browser if enabled. If enabled, this policy also affects the import dialog.

Import browsing history from default browser on first run -- This policy forces the browsing history to be imported from the current default browser if enabled. If enabled, this policy also affects the import dialog.
Import of homepage from default browser on first run -- This policy forces the home page to be imported from the current default browser if enabled.

Import saved passwords from default browser on first run -- This policy forces the saved passwords to be imported from the previous default browser if enabled. If enabled, this policy also affects the import dialog.

Import search engines from default browser on first run -- This policy forces search engines to be imported from the current default browser if enabled. If enabled, this policy also affects the import dialog.

Enable Incognito -- This policy is deprecated. Please, use IncognitoModeAvailability instead. Enables Incognito mode in Google Chrome. If this setting is enabled or not configured, users can open web pages in incognito mode.
Incognito mode availability -- Specifies whether the user may open pages in Incognito mode in Google Chrome.

Enable Intensive Wake Up Throttling -- When enabled, the IntensiveWakeUpThrottling feature causes JavaScript timers in background tabs to be aggressively throttled and coalesced, running no more than once per minute after a page has been backgrounded for 5 minutes or more.
Enable Site Isolation for specified origins -- If the policy is enabled, each of the named origins in a comma-separated list will run in its own process.
Javascript Enabled -- This policy is deprecated, please use DefaultJavaScriptSetting instead. Can be used to disabled JavaScript in Google Chrome.

Enable chrome://devices -- This policy controls access to controllable features in the local discovery UI (chrome://devices) which shows discoverable devices near the user as well as cloud devices registered to them.

Suppress lookalike domain warnings on domains -- This policy prevents the display of lookalike URL warnings on the sites listed. These warnings are typically shown on sites that Google Chrome believes might be trying to spoof another site the user is familiar with.

keys.description: Maximal number of concurrent connections to the proxy server -- Specifies the maximal number of simultaneous connections to the proxy server.
Maximum fetch delay after a policy invalidation -- Specifies the maximum delay in milliseconds between receiving a policy invalidation and fetching the new policy from the device management service.

Enable Media Recommendations -- By default the browser will show media recommendations that are personalized to the user. Setting this policy to Disabled will result in these recommendations being hidden from the user.

Allow Google Cast to connect to Cast devices on all IP addresses. -- If this policy is set to true, Google Cast will connect to Cast devices on all IP addresses, not just RFC1918/RFC4913 private addresses.
Enable reporting of usage and crash-related data -- Enables anonymous reporting of usage and crash-related data about Google Chrome to Google and prevents users from changing this setting.

allowedValueTitles: Predict network actions on any network connection
Predict network actions on any network that is not cellular.
Do not predict network actions on any network connection
keys.description: Enable network prediction -- (Deprecated in 50, removed in 52. After 52, if value 1 is set, it will be treated as 0 - predict network actions on any network connection.) Enables network prediction in Google Chrome and prevents users from changing this setting.
Show cards on the New Tab Page -- This policy controls the visibility of cards on the New Tab Page. Cards surface entry points to launch common user journeys based on the user's browsing behavior.
Allow New Tab page background customization -- Allow users to customize the background on the New Tab page
Origins or hostname patterns to be treated as secure context. -- The policy specifies a list of origins (URLs) or hostname patterns (such as "*.example.com") to be treated as secure contexts.
Payment Method Query -- Allows you to set whether websites are allowed to check if the user has payment methods saved.
Enable Policy Atomic Groups -- Enables the concept of policy atomic groups.

Allow merging dictionary policies from different sources -- Allows the selected policies to be merged when they come from different sources, with the same scopes and level. Entered strings must match a Chrome policy / key name that uses a dictionary for its data type.

Allow merging list policies from different sources -- Allows the selected policies to be merged when they come from different sources, with the same scopes and level. Entered strings must match a Chrome policy / key name that use an array (list) of strings for its data type.

Policy Refresh Rate -- Refresh rate for user policy. Specifies the period in milliseconds at which the device management service is queried for user policy information. Setting this policy overrides the default value of 3 hours.
Profile picker availabily on startup -- Specifies whether the profile picker is enabled, disabled or forced at the browser startup.
Enable showing full-tab promotional content -- Allows you to control the presentation of full-tab promotional and/or educational content in Google Chrome.

Ask where to save each file before downloading -- If the policy is enabled, the user will be asked where to save each file before downloading. If the policy is disabled, downloads will start immediately, and the user will not be asked where to save the file.
Allow QUIC protocol -- If this policy is set to true or not set usage of QUIC protocol in Google Chrome is allowed. If this policy is set to false usage of QUIC protocol is disallowed.

allowedValueTitles: Show a recurring prompt to the user indicating that a relaunch is recommended
Show a recurring prompt to the user indicating that a relaunch is required
keys.description: Notify a user that a browser relaunch is recommended or required -- Notify users that Google Chrome must be relaunched to apply a pending update.

Update time period -- Allows you to set the time period, in milliseconds, over which users are notified that Google Chrome must be relaunched or that a Google Chrome OS device must be restarted to apply a pending update.
Allow remote debugging -- Controls whether users may use remote debugging.
Restrict which users are allowed to sign in to Google Chrome -- Contains a regular expression which is used to determine which users can sign in to Google Chrome.

Extend Flash content setting to all content -- If you enable this setting, all Flash content embedded on websites that have been set to allow Flash in content settings -- either by the user or by enterprise policy -- will be run, including content from other origins or small content.
Safe Browsing checks -- Setting the policy to Enabled or leaving it unset means downloaded files are sent to be analyzed by Safe Browsing, even when it's from a trusted source.

allowedValueTitles: Do not filter sites for adult content
Filter top level sites (but not embedded iframes) for adult content
keys.description: Control SafeSites adult content filtering. -- This policy controls the application of the SafeSites URL filter. This filter uses the Google Safe Search API to classify URLs as pornographic or not.
Disable saving browser history -- Disables saving browser history in Google Chrome and prevents users from changing this setting.

Screen Capture -- If enabled or not configured (default), a Web page can use screen-share APIs (e.g., getDisplayMedia() or the Desktop Capture extension API) to prompt the user to select a tab, window or desktop to capture.

Enable scroll to text fragment -- This feature allows for hyperlinks and address bar URL navigations to target specific text within a web page, which will be scrolled to once the loading of the web page is complete.
Enable search suggestions -- Enables search suggestions in Google Chrome's omnibox and prevents users from changing this setting.

URLs/domains automatically permitted direct Security Key attestation -- Specifies URLs and domains for which no prompt will be shown when attestation certificates from Security Keys are requested. Additionally, a signal will be sent to the Security Key indicating that individual attestation may be used.
Enable Shared Clipboard -- Enables the Shared Clipboard feature which allows users to send text between Chrome Desktops and an Android device when Sync is enabled and the user is Signed-in.
Show the apps shortcut in the bookmark bar -- Enables or disables the apps shortcut in the bookmark bar.
Show Full URLs -- This feature enables display of the full URL in the address bar. If this policy is set to True, then the full URL will be shown in the address bar, including schemes and subdomains.
Enabled Signed HTTP Exchange (SXG) support -- Enable support for Signed HTTP Exchange (SXG).
Allow sign in -- This policy is deprecated, consider using BrowserSignin instead. Allows the user to sign in to Google Chrome.
Enable signin interception -- This settings enables or disables signin interception.

Enable Site Isolation for every site -- You might want to look at the IsolateOrigins policy setting to get the best of both worlds, isolation and limited impact for users, by using IsolateOrigins with a list of the sites you want to isolate.

Enable or disable spell checking web service -- Google Chrome can use a Google web service to help resolve spelling errors. If this setting is enabled, then this service is always used. If this setting is disabled, then this service is never used.
Enable spellcheck -- If this policy is not set or enabled, the user is allowed to use spellcheck.

Allow proceeding from the SSL warning page -- Chrome shows a warning page when users navigate to sites that have SSL errors. By default or when this policy is set to true, users are allowed to click through these warning pages.
Minimum SSL version enabled -- If this policy is not configured then Google Chrome uses a default minimum version which is TLS 1.0.
Enable strict MIME type checking for worker scripts -- This policy enables strict MIME type checking for worker scripts.
Stricter Mixed Content Treatment -- This policy controls the treatment for mixed content (HTTP content in HTTPS sites) in the browser.
Suppress the unsupported OS warning -- Suppresses the warning that appears when Google Chrome is running on a computer or operating system that is no longer supported.
Disable synchronization of data with Google -- Disables data synchronization in Google Chrome using Google-hosted synchronization services and prevents users from changing this setting.
Sync types to disable -- If this policy is set, all specified data types will be excluded from synchronization both for Google Sync as well as for roaming profile synchronization.

subkeys.description: Data Types

keys.description: Do not set window.opener for links targeting _blank -- Setting the policy to Disabled allows popups targeting _blank to access (via JavaScript) the page that requested to open the popup.
Enable ending processes in Task Manager -- If set to false, the 'End process' button is disabled in the Task Manager.

Enable TLS 1.3 hardening for local anchors -- Enable a TLS 1.3 security feature for local trust anchors. This policy controls a security feature in TLS 1.3 which protects connections against downgrade attacks.

Total Memory Limit -- Configures the amount of memory that a single Google Chrome instance can use before tabs start being discarded (I.E. the memory used by the tab will be freed and the tab will have to be reloaded when switched to) to save memory.
Enable Translate -- Enables the integrated Google Translate service on Google Chrome.
URL Blacklist -- This policy prevents the user from loading web pages from blacklisted URLs. The denylist provides a list of URL patterns that specify which URLs will be denied.
URL Blocklist -- This policy prevents the user from loading web pages from blocked URLs. The blocklist provides a list of URL patterns that specify which URLs will be denied.

Allow access to a list of URLs -- Allows access to the listed URLs, as exceptions to the URL denylist. A URL pattern is formatted according to https://www.chromium.org/administrators/url-blacklist-filter-format.

Allow access to a list of URLs -- Allows access to the listed URLs, as exceptions to the URL block list. A URL pattern is formatted according to https://www.chromium.org/administrators/url-blacklist-filter-format.

Origins or hostname patterns for which restrictions on insecure origins should not apply -- Deprecated in M69. Use OverrideSecurityRestrictionsOnInsecureOrigin instead. The policy specifies a list of origins (URLs) or hostname patterns (such as "*.example.com") for which security restrictions on insecure origins will not apply.
Enable URL-keyed anonymized data collection -- Enable URL-keyed anonymized data collection in Google Chrome and prevents users from changing this setting.
Enable user agent client hints -- When enabled the User-Agent Client Hints feature sends granular request headers providing information about the user browser and environment.
Allow user feedback -- Allow user feedback. If the policy is set to false, users can not send feedback to Google.

Set user data directory -- Configures the directory that Google Chrome will use for storing user data. See https://www.chromium.org/administrators/policy-list-3/user-data-directory-variables for a list of variables that can be used.

User data snapshot retention limit -- Limits the number of user data snapshots retained for use in case of emergency rollback. If this policy is not set, the default value of 3 is used. If the policy is set to 0, no snapshots will be taken.

Allow or deny video capture -- If enabled or not configured (default), the user will be prompted for video capture access except for URLs configured in the VideoCaptureAllowedUrls list which will be granted access without prompting.

URLs that will be granted access to video capture devices without prompt -- Patterns in this list will be matched against the security origin of the requesting URL. If a match is found, access to audio capture devices will be granted without prompt.
WebApp Force Install List -- Specifies a list of websites that are installed silently, without user interaction, and which cannot be uninstalled nor disabled by the user.

Allow WebDriver to Override Incompatible Policies -- This policy allows users of the WebDriver feature to override policies which can interfere with its operation.

Allow legacy TLS/DTLS downgrade in WebRTC -- f enabled, WebRTC peer connections can downgrade to obsolete versions of the TLS/DTLS (DTLS 1.0, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1) protocols. When this policy is disabled or not set, these TLS/DTLS versions are disabled.

Allow collection of WebRTC event logs from Google services -- If the policy is set to true, Google Chrome is allowed to collect WebRTC event logs from Google services (e.g. Google Meet), and upload those logs to Google.

Native Messaging Host Blocklist -- Allows you to specify which native messaging hosts that should not be loaded. A block list value of '*' means all native messaging hosts are denied unless they are explicitly listed in the allow list.
Allow user-level Native Messaging hosts (installed without admin permissions) -- Enables user-level installation of Native Messaging hosts.

Native Messaging Host Whitelist -- Allows you to specify which native messaging hosts are not subject to the blacklist. A blacklist value of * means all native messaging hosts are denied and only native messaging hosts listed in the whitelist will be loaded.

Native Messaging Host Allowlist -- Allows you to specify which native messaging hosts are not subject to the block list. A block list value of * means all native messaging hosts are denied and only native messaging hosts listed in the allow list will be loaded.
Enable password leak detection -- This policy can be used to force enable or force disable credential leak checking in Google Chrome.
Enable saving passwords to the password manager -- If this setting is enabled, users can have Google Chrome memorize passwords and provide them automatically the next time they log in to a site.
Enable Google Cloud Print proxy -- Enables Google Chrome to act as a proxy between Google Cloud Print and legacy printers connected to the machine.

Enable submission of documents to Google Cloud Print -- Enables Google Chrome to submit documents to Google Cloud Print for printing. NOTE: This only affects Google Cloud Print support in Google Chrome. It does not prevent users from submitting print jobs on web sites.
Default printer selection rules -- Overrides Google Chrome default printer selection rules.
Disable Print Preview -- Show the system print dialog instead of print preview.
Print Headers & Footers -- Force 'headers and footers' to be on or off in the printing dialog.
Printer Type Deny List -- The printers of types placed on the deny list will be disabled from being discovered or having their capabilities fetched.

Use System Default Printer as Default -- Causes Google Chrome to use the system default printer as the default choice in Print Preview instead of the most recently used printer.

Enable or disable PIN-less authentication for remote access hosts -- If this setting is enabled or not configured, then users can opt to pair clients and hosts at connection time, eliminating the need to enter a PIN every time.

Allow remote access file transfer -- Controls the ability of a user connected to a remote access host to transfer files between the client and the host. This does not apply to remote assistance connections, which do not support file transfer.
Allow gnubby authentication for remote access hosts -- If this setting is enabled, then gnubby authentication requests will be proxied across a remote host connection.
Enable the use of relay servers by the remote access host -- Enables usage of relay servers when remote clients are trying to establish a connection to this machine.

Configure the required domain names for remote access clients -- Configure the required domain name for remote access clients. This policy is deprecated. Please use RemoteAccessHostClientDomainList instead.
Configure the required domain names for remote access clients -- Configures the required client domain names that will be imposed on remote access clients and prevents users from changing it.
Configure the required domain names for remote access hosts -- Configure the required domain name for remote access hosts. This policy is deprecated. Please use RemoteAccessHostDomainList instead.
Configure the required domain names for remote access hosts -- Configures the required host domain names that will be imposed on remote access hosts and prevents users from changing it.
Enable firewall traversal from remote access host -- Enables usage of STUN servers when remote clients are trying to establish a connection to this machine.

Require that the name of the local user and the remote access host owner match -- If this setting is enabled, then the remote access host compares the name of the local user (that the host is associated with) and the name of the Google account registered as the host owner (i.e. "johndoe" if the host is owned by…
Enable curtaining of remote access hosts -- Enables curtaining of remote access hosts while a connection is in progress.
Configure the TalkGadget prefix for remote access hosts -- Configures the TalkGadget prefix that will be used by remote access hosts and prevents users from changing it.

URL where remote access clients should obtain their authentication token -- If this policy is set, the remote access host will require authenticating clients to obtain an authentication token from this URL in order to connect. Must be used in conjunction with RemoteAccessHostTokenValidationUrl.

Client certificate for connecting to RemoteAccessHostTokenValidationUrl -- If this policy is set, the host will use a client certificate with the given issuer CN to authenticate to RemoteAccessHostTokenValidationUrl. Set it to "*" to use any available client certificate.

URL for validating remote access client authentication token -- If this policy is set, the remote access host will use this URL to validate authentication tokens from remote access clients, in order to accept connections. Must be used in conjunction with RemoteAccessHostTokenUrl.
Restrict the UDP port range used by the remote access host -- Restricts the UDP port range used by the remote access host in this machine.

Configure the change password URL. -- Configure the change password URL (HTTP and HTTPS schemes only). Password protection service will send users to this URL to change their password after seeing a warning in the browser.

Configure the list of enterprise login URLs where password protection service should capture fingerprint of password. -- Configure the list of enterprise login URLs (HTTP and HTTPS schemes only). Fingerprint of password will be captured on these URLs and used for password reuse detection.

keys.description: Password protection warning trigger -- Allows you to control the triggering of passwore protection warning. Password protection alerts users when they reuse their protected password on potentially suspicious sites.
Enable Safe Browsing -- Enables Google Chrome's Safe Browsing feature and prevents users from changing this setting.
Enable Safe Browsing Extended Reporting -- Enables Google Chrome's Safe Browsing Extended Reporting and prevents users from changing this setting.

allowedValueTitles: Safe Browsing is active in the standard mode
Safe Browsing is active in the enhanced mode
keys.description: Safe Browsing protection level -- Allows you to control whether Google Chrome's Safe Browsing feature is enabled and the mode it operates in. Safe Browsing 'enhanced' mode provides better security, but requires sharing more browsing information with Google.

Configure the list of domains on which Safe Browsing will not trigger warnings. -- Configure the list of domains which Safe Browsing will trust. This means: Safe Browsing will not check for dangerous resources (e.g. phishing, malware, or unwanted software) if their URLs match these domains.

Configure the list of domains on which Safe Browsing will not trigger warnings. -- Configure the list of domains which Safe Browsing will trust. This means: Safe Browsing will not check for dangerous resources (e.g. phishing, malware, or unwanted software) if their URLs match these domains.

Allow users to opt in to Safe Browsing extended reporting -- This setting is deprecated, use SafeBrowsingExtendedReportingEnabled instead. Enabling or disabling SafeBrowsingExtendedReportingEnabled is equivalent to setting SafeBrowsingExtendedReportingOptInAllowed to False.

Use New Tab Page as homepage -- Configures the type of the default home page in Google Chrome and prevents users from changing home page preferences. The home page can either be set to a URL you specify or set to the New Tab Page.
Home page URL -- Configures the default home page URL in Google Chrome and prevents users from changing it.
New Tab page URL -- Configures the default New Tab page URL and prevents users from changing it.

URLs to open on startup -- If 'Open a list of URLs' is selected as the startup action, this allows you to specify the list of URLs that are opened. If left not set no URL will be opened on start up.
Show Home button on toolbar -- Shows the Home button on Google Chrome's toolbar.
Allow WebUSB on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are allowed to ask the user to grant them access to a USB device.
Block WebUSB on these sites -- Allows you to set a list of url patterns that specify sites which are prevented from asking the user to grant them access to a USB device.
Control where Developer Tools can be used -- Disables the Developer Tools and the JavaScript console. This policy is deprecated in M68, please use DeveloperToolsAvailability instead.

keys.description: Allowed Accounts Pattern -- Regular expression indicating accounts that are allowed to sign in on this machine.
Auto Start on Login -- Start Drive for desktop automatically on session login.
Max Downstream Bandwidth -- Maximum downstream kilobytes per second.
Max Upstream Bandwidth -- Maximum upstream kilobytes per second.
Content Cache Path -- Sets the path to the content cache location on a connected APFS or HFS+ file system.
Max Content Cache Size -- Sets the limit on content cache size in kilobytes. The limit is capped at 20% of the available space on the hard drive regardless of the setting value.
Default Mount Point -- Set the mounted drive path. You can include tilde (~) or environment variables in the path.
Disable External Media Sync -- Disables backing up files and folders from external media, such as USB drives, cameras, and phones, to Google Drive or Google Photos.
Disable Localized Virtual Folders -- Disables localized names for My Drive, Shared drives, and Computers. Names remain in en-US instead of being localized to the OS system language.
Disable Outlook Meet Plugin -- Disables the Microsoft Outlook Meet plugin that's bundled with Drive for desktop.

Icon (Premium) -- Prodvide the file path to a JPEG or PNG to use as the icon in the Elevate24 application.
Heading (Premium) -- Change the standard header from Elevate24 in the application. Always displays in bold.
Sub Header (Premium) -- Change the standard text "Privilege Access Management" under the Elevate24 header. New UI V2.2.0+ Only.
Main Button Text (Premium) -- Change the standard button text from Elevate in the application.
Hide Powered By Jigsaw24 Logo (Premium) -- Hide the “Powered by Jigsaw24” logo in the application.

Disable User Elevation -- Elevate24 2.5+ Only. When enabled, the Elevate24 menubar UI is hidden and cannot be launched manually from /Applications. End users will have no visible way to request elevation, view their session status, or interact with Elevate24 directly.
Allow CLI Elevation -- Elevate24 2.5+ Only. When enabled, allows user to elevate from the command-line.
Enable Choice of Session Times -- Enables the option for the application to display a choice of times. To be used in conjuction with Session Times list.
Enable free text reason -- Will replace reasons drop down list with a free text entry box.
Block extending session -- Will disable the ability to extend the time of an active Elevate24 session.
Session Time -- Change the length of time (in seconds) the user will be elevated for. Do not use this key if you want to present a list of times to choose from.
Session Times -- List of available times to chose from in the Application. Enter time below in seconds.
Reasons -- The reasons to choose for needing elevated rights in dropbox within the application.
Advanced Reasons -- New reason type that can require a free-text note. Combined with the existing Reasons list. The selected reason is logged to Reason, the note to ReasonText.

Free Text Placeholder

keys.description: Set Session Expiry Notification (Premium) -- Set the number of minutes before the application notifies the user that the session is expiring

Allow User Defined Scripts -- Elevate24 2.4+ Only. When enabled, allows users to specify their own elevation and demotion script paths in addition to any admin-defined scripts. If scripts are configured at both the admin and user level, all scripts will execute.
Elevate Script Path -- Elevate24 2.4+ Only. Specify the full file path to a script that will be executed automatically when a user's session is elevated to admin.
Elevate Script Hash -- Elevate24 2.4+ Only. Optionally provide the SHA256 hash of the elevation script specified in ElevateScriptPath.
Demote Script Path -- Elevate24 2.4+ Only. Specify the full file path to a script that will be executed automatically when a user's elevated session ends and they are demoted back to a standard user.
Demote Script Hash -- Elevate24 2.4+ Only. Optionally provide the SHA256 hash of the demotion script specified in DemoteScriptPath.

Elevation Cooldown (Minutes) -- Enforces a wait between elevations: once a session ends the machine cannot re-elevate for a configurable period. Enforced per-computer inside the system extension (covers UI, CLI, and automatic session expiry), and resistant to clock tampering.

Offline Cooldown Override -- Lets a helpdesk grant a one-time, short code that clears an active cooldown while the device is offline. Uses a Secure Enclave key so no reusable secret is stored on the device; codes are single-use and rate-limited.
Offline Cooldown Override Message -- Custom helpdesk contact text shown in the offline cooldown override popover. If unset, a built-in message is used.
Disable Default Log (Premium) -- To disable sending of premium reporting data to Jigsaw24. If you are a basic customer, no data is sent from the device, it is all stored locally.
SIEM URL (Premium)
SIEM Auth Header (Premium)
SIEM Auth Token (Premium)
Format Log Message for Splunk (Premium) -- Enable to ensure correct formatting of logs when using Splunk as the endpoint. Available in Elevate24 2.6.0 and later.

keys.description: Enable Session Monitoring (Premium) -- To enable monitoring of administrator activities whilst in an elevated state.
Apple Auth -- Prompts the user for their local Apple credentials or TouchID (if enabled on device) before allowing elevation.
OTP Auth (Premium) -- Enables the use of authenticator applications such as Google Auth or Microsoft Auth, prompting for a valid session token before Elevating to admin.
Standard At Load -- Will remove admin rights when the application first launches.

Demote All Admin -- Enables all admin users being demoted to standard users when the current elevation period ends. If you have any accounts on the device you'd like to remain admin please configure Demote Exclusions.
Demote All Admin Quit -- Will demote all admin accounts from admin when the application quits or the laptop is restarted.
Demote Exclusions -- Will exclude accounts on device from being demoted.
Kill Terminal Sessions -- Will demote the current terminal session from sudo session to standard.
System Extension -- Elevate24 v2.3+ Only. To ensure the Application is protected by the on-device system extension, to prevent misuse and tampering.
User Elevate Admin (Premium) -- Will create a temporary secondary account instead of Elevating the primary account. A temporary password will also be supplied upon elevation.

Use Current User As Admin (Premium) -- If User Elevate Admin Key is enabled and this key is also enabled, the temporary account will use the current logged in users username as part of the account naming. For example, Joe.Bloggs-adm
Admin User Name (Premium) -- If ‘Use Current User As Admin’ is not enabled, this key allows the ability to create a temporary admin account with a standard name. Such as "Temp Admin"
Complex Password (Premium) -- Enables the use of a custom complex password when 'User Elevate Admin' is enabled.
Password Uppercase (Premium) -- Enter the amount of uppercase Letters required for the password.
Password Lowercase (Premium) -- Enter the amount of lowercase Letters required for the password.
Password Numbers (Premium) -- Enter the amount of numbers required for the password.
Password Symbols (Premium) -- Enter the amount of symbols required for the password.

Show Admin Password Grace (Premium) -- Set the number of seconds after elevation or last showing the password that the password will be shown (Max 45 seconds). This only works if 'User Elevate Admin' is enabled.

entries.title: S.U.P.E.R.M.A.N
entries.description: Use this section to define settings for S.U.P.E.R.M.A.N (super)

keys.description: Auth Ask User To Save Password -- Prompt the end user to save their password which can then be used to authenticate the local softwareupdate command
Auth Credential Failover To User -- If any managed automatic authentication method fails validation, then failover to local end user authentication
Auth Jamf Computer ID -- Use this when using super with Jamf Pro API account
Jamf Custom URL Override -- Allows you to override the default Jamf Pro management URL for a custom Jamf Pro API URL

User Authentication MDM Failover -- The MDM workflow can be unreliable due to its complexity, and super will automatically try again upon failure, however this settings allows super to try other options
Focus Count Deadline -- The maximum number of automatic deferrals allowed if the system is in user-enabled Focus/Do Not Disturb or when a process has requested that the display not go to sleep
Hard Count Deadline -- The maximum number of user selected deferrals allowed before the computer automatically restarts for updates without asking the user for approval
Soft Count Deadline -- The maximum number of user selected deferrals allowed before showing a soft deadline dialog

Focus Date Deadline -- This is the last date and time when automatic deferrals are allowed if the system is in user-enabled Focus/Do Not Disturb or when a process has requested that the display not go to sleep (for example, during an active meeting)
Hard Date Deadline -- If this date has passed, the computer restarts and udpates without asking the user for approval
Soft Date Deadline -- If this date and time have passed, an interactive update restart dialog appears indicating that no more user deferrals are allowed

Focus Days Deadline -- The maximum number of days that automatic deferrals are allowed if the system is in user-enabled Focus/Do Not Disturb or when a process has requested that the display not go to sleep (for example, during an active meeting).
Hard Days Deadline -- The maximum number of days allowed before the computer automatically restarts for updates without asking the user for approval
Soft Days Deadline -- The maximum number of days allowed before the soft deadline dialog. The soft deadline is an interactive update restart dialog indicating that no more deferrals are allowed

Focus Defer Timer -- The number of minutes to defer the update restart dialog automatically if a process has prevented display sleep (for example, during an active meeting) or the user has Focus or Do Not Disturb enabled
Default Dialog Timeout -- Sets the default timeout for any dialog that doesn't have a specific timeout setting
Free Space Timeout -- Timeout for computers with not enough free space
Battery Timeout -- Timeout for computers where power is required
Soft Display Timeout -- Sets an automatic timeout for interactive update restart dialogs in seconds
User Authentication Timeout -- On Mac computers with Apple Silicon, the number of seconds to wait for the user to successfully authenticate when presented with the user authenticated dialog
User Choice Dialog Timeout -- Sets an automatic timeout for the user choice (restart/install or defer) dialog in seconds
User Scheduled Install User Choice Dialog Timeout -- Sets an automatic timeout for the scheduled install user choice dialog in seconds
Default Accessory File -- Local path or http(s) URL to a file that is the default accessory

Jamf Policy Accessory File -- Local path or http(s) URL to a file that is the accessory to display when the InstallJamfPolicyTriggers payload option is also enabled and the workflow target is only Jamf Pro Policy Triggers
Major Upgrades Accessory File -- Local path or http(s) URL to a file that is the accessory to display when performing macOS upgrades
Minor Updates Updates Accessory File -- Local path or http(s) URL to a file that is the accessory to display when performing macOS updates

Non-System Updates Accessory File -- Local path or http(s) URL to a file that is the accessory to display when the InstallNonSystemUpdatesWithoutRestarting payload option is also enabled and the workflow target is only non-system updates

Restart Without Updates Accessory File -- Local path or http(s) URL to a file that is the accessory to display when the WorkflowRestartWithoutUpdates payload option is also enabled and the workflow target is only a forced restart without any updates
Custom Display Accessory -- Interactive dialogs (but not notifications) generated by IBM Notifier can be easily customized via several display accessory options
Help Button -- Plain text to display or http(s) URL link to follow for the Help Button
Display Hide Progress Bar -- This option hides the animated progress bar (as opposed showing it) for notifications and alerts
Dark Display Icon -- Local path or http(s) URL to a file that is the picture to display in notifications or dialogs when in dark mode. Failover to DisplayIconFile payload if configured
Light Display Icon -- Local path or http(s) URL to a file that is the picture to display in notifications or dialogs when in light mode. Failover to DisplayIconFile payload if configured
Display Icon -- Local path or http(s) URL to a file that is the picture to display in notifications or dialogs
Display Icon Size -- Number of pixels for the DisplayIcon in IBM Notifier dialogs

Install Jamf Policy Triggers -- If a restart is required for system updates or forced via RestartWithoutUpdates, this list of Jamf Policy Triggers runs before any available updates install and the computer restarts
Install Jamf Policies Without A Restart -- Allows for installation of Jamf Pro Policies even if there are no available macOS updates/upgrades
Apple Zero Day Workflow Date -- Leverages the public MacAdmin's SOFA macOS machine readable JSON feed to discover release dates for use in workflows with deadline day options
Scheduled Install User Choice -- Adds a Schedule button to the standard deferral dialog
Test Mode -- Mode to validate parameters, credentials, notifications, dialogs, deferrals, and deadline logic
Start Workflow Immediately -- Kicks off the super workflow immediately, prompting user that an update has begun
Schedule Workflow Active -- Allows you to define multiple weekday time frames that specify when the super workflow is allowed to be active (aka maintenance windows)
Test Battery Level -- Minmum Battery Percentage
Test Mode Timeout -- The amount of time in seconds to leave test notifications and dialogs open before moving on in the workflow
Free Space Update -- Free space required for updates
Test Free Space Upgrade -- Free space required for upgrades
Manual Zero Day Workflow Date -- Instead of having the days deadline counter, automatically select the day zero date
Apple Zero Day Custom URL -- Allows for a custom self-hosted MacAdmin's SOFA macOS machine readable JSON feed
Scheduled Install Date -- Allows you to specify a date and time that a scheduled installation takes place
Scheduled Install Days -- Allows you to specify the number of days after the zero date that a scheduled installation takes place

Scheduled Install Reminder -- Allows you to specify a list of minutes separated by commas (no spaces) that define how often a scheduled installation reminder dialog appears prior to a scheduled installation
Deferral Timer Default -- The number of minutes to defer until the next update workflow attempt if a user choses not restart
Deferral Timer Error -- The number of minutes to defer if super detects an error in the workflow (for example, network or MDM connectivity issues)
Deferral Timer Menu -- Display a deferral time pop-up menu in the non-deadline restart dialog that allows the user to override the Deferral Timer Default timer

Deferral Timer Workflow Relaunch -- The number of minutes to defer if no software updates are available or allowed. Enabling this option results in super acting as a permanent agent that checks for software updates on a regular basis
Display Hide Background -- Hide the background while displaying super dialogs and notifications
Display Notifications Centered -- Display super notifications in the center of the screen
Display Silently -- Do not play the system alert sound when opening super dialogs and notifications
Display Unmovable -- Disable the users ability to move super dialogs and notifications
Display Warning Button String -- A plain text string or URL to open when the user clicks the warning button (exclamation mark icon) in all interactive dialogs (but not notifications)

Install macOS Major Upgrades -- With this option enabled super leverages built-in commands and the mist command to find compatible macOS major upgrade versions. If a newer macOS major upgrade is available then the super workflow attempts to download and install the upgrade.
Restart Without Updates -- Force a restart even if Apple software updates do not need it

Install MacOS Major Version Target -- Limit the installation of macOS major upgrade versions to the major (whole number) version specified in this option. This option requires that you have also specified the InstallMacOSMajorUpgrades option

Install Non System Updates Without Restarting -- If there are no pending restart-required macOS updates or upgrades, make the super workflow install non-system Apple software updates as soon as they become available
Install Rapid Security Responses -- Allow the super workflow to install macOS Rapid Security Response (RSR) updates
Install macOS BSI Update -- Allows the super workflow to install macOS BSI Updates
Workflow Disable Relaunch -- Disable the automatic relaunch of the super workflow when no macOS updates or upgrades are available or allowed
Workflow Disable Update Check -- Disable the super workflow from checking for, downloading, or installing any Apple software updates or upgrades, even if they are available
Workflow Only Download -- Download and prepare macOS updates or upgrades but do not start any installation workflow
Verbose Mode -- Mode to generate additional log output
Suppress Terms of Services and Privacy Prompt -- Enable this option to automatically accept the Privacy Policy and Terms of Service for users.
Enable Automatic Update Checks -- Automatically check for The Unarchiver (Standalone) updates

keys.description: Sparkle Feed URL -- Setting this to a non-existent URL will disable the ability for users to manually check for updates. Useful when you intend to use your own software distribution mechanism to deploy updates.
Enable Automatic Update Checks -- Controls automatic update checks.
Automatic Update Check Interval -- Controls the automatic update check interval. The default is 1 day (86400 seconds). Setting to 0 disables updates.

Automatic Update Install Prompt -- Controls the automatic update install prompt. When enabled, presents users with the option to allow automatic download and install of available updates. If disabled, disallows automatic updates and requires manual installation every time.
Enable Automatic Silent Updates -- Controls automatic silent updates. If enabled, users will not be informed about updates and updates will be silently installed when the app quits.
Skipped Version Updates -- Controls which update versions should be suppressed upon launching Rhinoceros

allowedValueTitles: Required And Optional Data (removed in version 4.70)
keys.description: Acknowledged Data Collection Policy -- The first time Version 4.12 or later of Microsoft AutoUpdate is launched, users will see a Required Data Notice dialog which provides them with information about what data from MAU is sent to Microsoft.
Channel Name -- Set the update channel that is used to check for updates. Click the documentation link for more information about which channel to use.
Disable Insider Checkbox -- Set this option to disable the "Join the Office Insider Program..." checkbox.
Enable Check for Updates Button -- Disable this option to make the "Check for Updates" button in unavailable.
Enable Extended Logging -- Enabled extended logging for Microsoft AutoUpdate operations. Writes logs to: /Library/Logs/Microsoft/autoupdate.log

allowedValueTitles: Automatically check for and install updates: "AutomaticDownload"
keys.description: How to Check for Updates -- Control how updates are checked for and handled.

Manifest Server -- Force Microsoft AutoUpdate to pull collateral using a custom server. This is good when enterprise wants to have strict control on which version of Office applications get installed.
Start Daemon on App Launch -- Enable this option to trigger the MAU Daemon when other Office applications are launched.
Ignore UI Open After Install -- Enable this option to prevent MAU UI from launching after install.
Disable Opt-In Notification -- When Set to TRUE, prevents Opt-In notification/pop-up window from showing even when HowToCheck is set to Automatic.

Update Cache Server -- Force Microsoft AutoUpdate to pull update binaries from a custom server. This is good when internet bandwidth is limited. Ensure that a trailing slash is used when specifying the value as this is mandatory.
Update Check Interval -- Specifies the number of minutes between checking for updates. Default is set to check every 13 hours.
Update Check Frequency -- Change how often the Microsoft AutoUpdate daemon will look for updates. The default is 720 minutes (12 hrs). By reducing this value MAU will look for updates sooner.
Update Deadline: Days Before Forced Quit -- Force quit applications and update X number of days after MAU first detects the update on each computer.
Update Deadline: Final Countdown Timer -- How many minutes is the final countdown timer once the update deadline is reached.

Update Deadline: Start Automatic Updates -- How many days in advance of the deadline that Automatic Download and Install mode begins. Temporarily overrides "HowToCheck" with "AutomaticDownload" until all updates are applied.

Updater Optimization -- If you have a security agent like CrowdStrike installed and updates cause beachballs; Set UpdaterOptimization preference to "CPU" to prefer file-based delta updates (instead of binary deltas). The trade-off will be larger monthly updates.
Global Deferral Days -- Global number of days after a release for which updates and offers to update will be postponed.
App Specific Deferral -- Number of days after a release for which updates and offers to update will be postponed, per individual app. This setting takes precedence over the global setting.

subkeys.description: App Specific Deferral Days -- Number of days after a release for which updates and offers to update will be postponed, per individual app. This setting takes precedence over the global setting.

Sign In Options -- Prevent users from signing in to any O365 service. This has the added effect of making sure users store no data online via microsoft servers.
Suppress 'Connected Services' dialog -- Disable the "Connected Services" dialog for MSA-based (personal) accounts.

keys.description: AutoUpdate -- Prevents Missive from automatically checking for updates to its Electron core. (Users will still see periodic requests to "update" via reload.)
Client Mode -- The client mode that Santa should operate in.
Deny on Read Error -- Deny execution in LOCKDOWN mode if there is an error reading or processing an executable file.
File Changes Regex -- Path regexes (ICU format) to monitor for file changes.
File Changes Prefix Filters -- Path prefixes to exclude from file change logging.

subkeys.description: Path Prefix

keys.description: Telemetry -- Types of telemetry events that should be logged.
Allowed Path Regex -- Path regexes (ICU format) of binaries to allow. Lower precedent than binary, certificate, and Team ID scopes.
Blocked Path Regex -- Path regexes (ICU format) of binaries to block. Lower precedent than binary, certificate, and Team ID scopes.
Bad Signature Protection -- Block binaries with a bad signing chain, unless explicitly allowed.
Enable Page Zero Protection -- Block 32-bit binaries missing the __PAGEZERO segment, unless explicitly allowed.
Enable Transitive Rules -- Allow transitive rules created by compiler-type rules.
Static Rules -- A static set of rules that always apply to the host, taking precedence over any rules configured by a sync server.

subkeys.description: Rule

Identifier -- The identifier for this rule. The required format depends on rule_type: • BINARY / CERTIFICATE — SHA-256 hash (64 hex characters) • TEAMID — 10-character alphanumeric Team ID (e.g. ZMCG7MLDV9) • SIGNINGID — TeamID:SigningID (e.g.
Rule Type -- The type of rule. Also determines the required format of the identifier and the rule's evaluation precedence: CDHash → Binary → SigningID → Certificate → TeamID.
Policy -- The action to take when this rule matches an execution.

CEL Expression -- A CEL (Common Expression Language) expression to evaluate when this rule matches. Required when policy is CEL. The expression receives an ExecutionContext and must return either a ReturnValue or a bool (true = ALLOWLIST, false = BLOCKLIST).

Custom Message -- Custom message to display in the block notification when this rule blocks an execution. Overrides the global BannedBlockMessage for this specific rule. Only applies to BLOCKLIST and SILENT_BLOCKLIST policies.

Custom URL -- A custom URL for the block notification button, overriding the global EventDetailURL for this specific rule. Supports the same substitution placeholders as EventDetailURL (e.g. %file_identifier%, %machine_id%, %username%).
Comment -- A freeform comment or note about this rule for documentation purposes. Ignored by Santa at runtime.

keys.description: Enable Silent Mode -- Disable all GUI notifications.
Enable Silent TTY Mode -- Disable all TTY (terminal) notifications.
Enable Menu Item -- Show the Santa menu bar item.
About Text -- Custom text to display at launch.
More Info URL -- Optional "More Info..." link.
Event Detail URL -- The URL to open when the user gets a block notification. If unset, the button will not be displayed.
Event Detail Text -- The text of the button for Event Detail URL.
File Access Event Detail URL -- The URL to open when the user gets a file access block notification. If unset, the button will not be displayed.
File Access Event Detail Text -- The text of the button for File Access Event Detail URL.
Unknown Block Message -- Custom message when an unknown binary is blocked.
Dismiss Text -- The text to display on the button that dismisses the binary block dialog.
Banned Block Message -- Custom message when a binary is blocked by a rule.
Monitor Notification Text -- Custom message when entering MONITOR mode.
Lockdown Notification Text -- Custom message when entering LOCKDOWN mode.
Standalone Notification Text -- Custom message when entering STANDALONE mode. (undocumented)
Banned USB Block Message -- Custom message when a Removable Media (e.g. USB device) is prevented from being mounted.
Remount USB Block Message -- Custom message when a Removable Media (e.g. USB device) is allowed to be mounted with a subset of the requested flags as defined by RemountUSBMode.
File Access Block Message -- Custom message when a file access is blocked by a rule.
Enable Notification Silences -- Allow users to silence notifications.
Branding Company Name -- Company name displayed in Santa UI. For GUI windows, this setting is ignored if BrandingCompanyLogo is set.

Branding Company Logo -- A URL referencing a logo image to display on Santa UIs. The image will be scaled down appropriately to fit within image bounds (currently 84x28 pixels). If set, this overrides BrandingCompanyName.

Branding Company Logo (Dark Mode) -- A URL referencing a logo image to display on Santa UIs. When the UI is displayed in dark mode and this is set, it overrides both BrandingCompanyLogo and BrandingCompanyName. Supported URL schemes: file:// and data:. HTTP/HTTPS URLs are not supported.
Fun Fonts On Specific Days -- Enable themed fonts and images on April 1, May 4 and October 31.
Sync Server URL
Enable Proto Transfer -- Enable binary proto transfer for sync instead of JSON.

Sync Proxy Configuration -- Proxy configuration applied to all network requests made during syncing. This dictionary is passed directly to NSURLSessionConfiguration.connectionProxyDictionary. Keys are the kCFNetworkProxies* CFNetwork constants (e.g.
Enable Upload Clean Syncs -- Upload events to the sync server even if a clean sync is requested.
Client Certificate File Path -- Location of a PKCS#12 certificate to be used for sync authentication.
Client Certificate Password
Client Certificate Common Name -- The Common Name of a certificate in the System keychain to be used for sync authentication.
Client Certificate Issuer Common Name -- The Issuer Name of a certificate in the System keychain to be used for sync authentication.
Server Authentication Certificate Roots -- X.509 certificate (.pem) for inclusion on device. A valid PEM containing one or more certificates to be used for certificate pinning.
Server Authentication Certificate Roots (Local) -- Path to an on-disk X.509 certificate (.pem). A valid PEM containing one or more certificates to be used for certificate pinning.
Machine Owner
Machine Owner Groups -- Groups the machine owner is a member of.
Machine ID
Machine Owner Plist -- The path to a plist that contains the MachineOwnerKey / value pair.
Machine Owner Key -- The key to use on Machine Owner Plist.
Machine Owner Groups Key -- The key to use on MachineOwnerPlist to access defined groups.
Machine ID Plist -- The path to a plist that contains the MachineIDKey / value pair.
Machine ID Key -- The key to use on Machine ID Plist.
Enable All Event Upload -- Upload all execution events to the sync server, including those explicitly allowed.
Disable Unknown Event Upload -- Do not upload events for executions of unknown binaries allowed in monitor mode.
Sync Client Content Encoding -- Content encoding used for sync requests.
Sync Extra Headers -- Dictionary of additional headers to include in all requests made to the sync server. System-managed headers such as Content-Length, Host, and WWW-Authenticate will be ignored.

subkeys.description: Header Value

keys.description: Event Log Type -- Defines how event logs are stored. Allowed values: syslog, file, protobuf, json, null. Note: the protobuf and JSON formats are in BETA and subject to change.
Event Log Path -- Path to the event log file (used for file/json logging).
Spool Directory -- Base directory for protobuf maildir-like logs.
Spool Max File Size -- Per-file size limit (KB) for protobuf spool files.
Spool Max Size -- Total size limit (MB) for protobuf spool directory.
Spool Max Event Buffer -- Maximum time (seconds) events are buffered before flushing to disk.
Enable Machine ID Decoration -- Appends the MachineID to the end of each log line if enabled.
Entitlements Prefix Filter -- Filters entitlements from execution telemetry by prefix. Entitlements are only logged when EventLogType is set to protobuf or json.
Entitlements Team ID Filter -- Filters entitlements from execution telemetry by Team ID. Entitlements are only logged when EventLogType is set to protobuf or json.
Telemetry Filter Expressions -- CEL expressions for filtering or redacting telemetry before upload. Only useful for Workshop customers.
Metric Format -- Format to export metrics as, supported formats are "rawjson" for a single JSON blob and "monarchjson" for a format consumable by Google's Monarch tooling.
Metric URL -- URL describing where monitoring metrics should be exported.
Metric Export Interval -- Time (seconds) between exporting metrics.
Metric Export Timeout -- Timeout (seconds) for exporting metrics.
Metric Extra Labels -- A map of key value pairs to add to all metric root labels. If a previously set key (e.g. host_name) is set to "" then the key is removed from the metric root labels.
Enable Standalone Password Fallback -- Enable password authorization fallback for Standalone mode.
Ignore Other Endpoint Security Clients -- Ignore events generated by other EndpointSecurity clients.
Enable Stats Collection -- Send basic stats to North Pole Security
Stats Organization ID -- North Pole Security customer ID for stats collection.
Anti Suspend Signing IDs -- A list of Signing IDs to protect from `pid_suspend` calls.
Allowed Santa Commands -- Array of allowed Santa commands. If unset, all commands are allowed; if set to an empty array, no commands are allowed.
Allow Delegated Signals -- Allow signals delegated by launchd on behalf of Apple platform binaries targeting santad.
File Access Policy Plist -- Path to a file access configuration plist.
File Access Policy -- A complete file access policy embedded directly in the Santa configuration. When set, FileAccessPolicyPlist is ignored.
File Access Policy Update Interval -- How often (in seconds) to re-read the file access policy config.
Override File Access Action -- Global override for the enforcement of all file access policy rules.
File Access Global Logs Per Second -- Average number of file access logs per second. Set to 0 to disable rate limiting.
File Access Global Window Size -- Window size over which the log rate limit is applied. Set to 0 to disable rate limiting.
Removable Media Action -- Action applied to all removable media devices.
Removable Media Remount Flags -- Mount flags applied when removable media is remounted.
Encrypted Removable Media Action -- Action applied to encrypted removable media devices.
Encrypted Removable Media Remount Flags -- Mount flags applied when encrypted removable media is remounted.
On Start USB Options -- Action applied to existing removable media when Santa starts.

keys.description: Managed Configuration (Base64 TOML) -- Base64-encoded TOML that supplies managed default configuration. It is applied as the highest-precedence configuration layer, above /etc/codex/managed_config.toml and the user's config.toml, so values set here override user settings.

Requirements (Base64 TOML) -- Base64-encoded TOML that supplies enforced requirements, such as allowed approval policies, sandbox modes, and MCP servers. Requirements constrain what users can configure.
Server Host -- FQDN taken from inside the square brackets in the file name of the client .dmg.
Server Port
Server Scheme
Skip Direct Print Monitor Tool
Strict SSL
Activation Experience -- Select a method for activating Parallels Desktop for Mac
License Key -- Enter your 30-character license key:
SSO Dialogue Header Text (Optional) -- Enter SSO dialogue header text:

SSO Dialogue Label Text (Optional) -- Enter SSO dialogue label text:

Sparkle Feed URL -- Setting this to a non-existent URL will disable the ability for users to manually check for updates. Useful when you intend to use your own software distribution mechanism to deploy updates.
Enable Automatic Update Checks -- Controls automatic update checks.
Automatic Update Check Interval -- Controls the automatic update check interval. The default is 1 day (86400 seconds). Setting to 0 disables updates.

Automatic Update Install Prompt -- Controls the automatic update install prompt. When enabled, presents users with the option to allow automatic download and install of available updates. If disabled, disallows automatic updates and requires manual installation every time.
Enable Automatic Silent Updates -- Controls automatic silent updates. If enabled, users will not be informed about updates and updates will be silently installed when the app quits.
Send Anonymous Profile Information -- When running software update checks, submit anonymous computer profile data to AirServer.
Use Lion-Style Full Screen -- Enable this setting if you want to use the native macOS fullscreen mode - slower.
User-Visible Device Name -- Use this field to override the name of the computer that appears on the AirPlay network.
User-Visible Lossless Recevier Device Name -- Only enable this preference when you wish to set a custom name for the device running AirServer in the AirPlay device list.
Launch at System Startup -- Have AirServer launch on system startup.
Audio Buffer Size -- Use this setting to tweak multi-room audio sync when streaming music from iTunes.
Password Type -- Choose authentication method when connecting to AirServer. While a Fixed Password is an available setting, it's not possible to define this password via profile.
Always on Top -- Enable this setting if you want AirServer windows to be on top of all other windows.

Enable Dual-Airplay Device -- This option creates a second AirPort Expresss-like audio receiver suffixed with an Ex. Streaming music to this endpoint will force the iOS device to stream your music in lossless quality.
Link iOS Device Volume -- If enabled, changing the volume on your iOS device will change the volume of your preferred output sound device; otherwise AirServer will lower the streaming music volume.

Optimize Mirroring for Device Type -- Here you can set the mirroring resolution AirServer provides to your iOS device. 'Retina' is recommended for all users, but if you are having connection problems, try the 1080p option.
Use Slow Network Mode -- Enabling this setting will lower the mirroring quality by half but uses four times less bandwidth.

Use Software Decoder Only -- Enable this setting if your AirPlay device regularly freezes or if you notice green artifacts when using AirPlay mirroring. This is common on older Macs that do not properly support hardware-accelerated video encoding.
Show in Dock -- Use this setting to toggle between running AirServer in the Dock and in the menu bar.

subkeys.description: Display Name -- The name you want to appear in SwiftDialog and logs. Initial Scripts will only be shown to the user if the item Fails.
Script Path -- A path to the script you want to run. Can be a local file path or a URL.
SHA256 -- The expected SHA256 of the script being run.

Retries -- The number of times Baseline will retry this specific item if it fails. If omitted, will use the Global Retries Default.

keys.description: WaitFor Timeout -- When using WaitFor, enter the number of seconds you wish to wait before Baseline considers remaining items a failure. This timer does not start until all other items are processed. Default if key is omitted is 600.
Force Restart -- This setting controls whether Baseline forces a restart after completion.
Force Log Out -- This setting controls whether Baseline forces a restart after completion.
Cleanup After Use -- This setting controls whether Baseline deletes it's install directory after use: /usr/local/Baseline.

Ignore Default Installomator Options -- By default, Baseline uses "NOTIFY=silent" and "BLOCKING_PROCESS_ACTION=kill" Installomator options. Setting this to True means Baseline will not use those options.
Skip Success Dialog -- If set to true, Baseline will not present a Success dialog at completion.
Skip Failure Dialog -- If set to true, Baseline will not present a Failure dialog at completion.
Silent Mode -- If set to true, no dialog windows will be created. All items and item types will process as normal.

Close List View Before Final Scripts -- If set to true, Baseline will close the list view window before running FinalScripts. Use this option if you want to utilize FinalScripts to have the user complete actions prior to the Baseline completion dialog.
Dialog List Window Options -- SwiftDialog options for the primary Baseline progress list window.
Dialog Success Window Options -- SwiftDialog options for the Success Dialog window.
Dialog Failure Window Options -- SwiftDialog options for the Failure Dialog window.
Dialog Inspect Mode Window Options -- SwiftDialog options for Inspect Mode. Most options should be in the JSON file, but some can be passed here. See swiftDialog documentation for specifics.

Inspect Mode JSON -- Path to your Inspect Mode JSON file. Using this option enables "Inspect Mode". DialogListView options will not be respected, and no Baseline DialogListView will be drawn. Inspect Mode is enabled after InitialScripts
Blur Screen -- This setting controls whether Baseline uses the SwiftDialog --blurscreen feature. Default is true. If you set to false, consider using --ontop in your DialogListOptions key

Show List -- If false, the ListView will not show any list items. Instead, a standard Dialog window is drawn with the options configured in `DialogListOptions`. If used with progress bar, the progress bar will still be displayed.
Show Progress Bar -- This setting controls whether Baseline displays a progress bar.
Show Display Names on Progress Bar -- This setting controls whether Baseline displays the current item being processed under the progress bar.
Use Installomator SwiftDialog Integration -- Tell Installomator to use it's built in SwiftDialog integration for the List View.
Verbose Jamf Items -- If set to true, when a Script is processing a jamf policy (/usr/local/bin/jamf), Baseline will watch the Jamf log to provide more verbose output on that line item.

Button 1 Enabled -- This setting enables SwiftDialog "Button 1" (the OK button) on the Baseline List View. This allows users to dismiss the list view and continue working while Baseline runs. By default this button is disabled.
Global Status Icon - Wait -- The icon used for the wait list status, if no specific wait status icon is set.
Global Status Icon - Success -- The icon used for the success list status, if no specific success status icon is set.
Global Status Icon - Fail -- The icon used for the fail list status, if no specific fail status icon is set.
Wait For Pending Icon -- The icon used for the "pending" status of all WaitFor items. Leave blank for nothing. Use "pending" for swiftDialog Default.

Reinstall SwiftDialog -- Deprecated: This feature was removed in v.2.3, as it is no longer needed. This setting controls whether Baseline will reinstall SwiftDialog as the final step before completion.

Exit Condition -- Define a file or folder path. When Baseline starts, if this file or folder exists, Baseline will exit quietly without processing any items. Use this option if your management tool may re-send scripts when not desired.
Bail Out File -- Define a file path. If this file exists at any point while Baseline is running, Baseline will exit and will not process additional items.
Default Installomator Retries -- Default number of retries for Installomator items. Default 0
Default Script Retries -- Default number of retries for Script items. Default 0
Default Package Retries -- Default number of retries for Package items. Default 0
Required Arguments -- There are four required arguments to make a valid Renew configuration.

subkeys.description: Maximum number of deferrals -- This is the maximum number of deferrals a user receives before Renew enters "Aggressive" mode. Set to '-1' to disable deferrals.
Uptime Threshold -- The number of days which a device is online prior to the Renew experience starting.
Notification Threshold -- The number of times the user will get a macOS Notification Center event prior to the full Swift Dialog experience. Set to '-1' to configure an infinite threshold.
Deferral Duration -- The minimum number of hours between when a user is notified that they need to restart.

Title -- The title of your dialog windows and notifications. Maps to the swiftDialog option: --title
Aggressive Message -- The message body you want in your Aggressive Mode dialog windows. Maps to SwiftDialog option: --message
Normal Message

Restart Button Text -- What do you want your "Restart Now" button to say? Maps to SwiftDialog option: --infobuttontext

Show Deferral Count -- If true, an additional sentence is added to your Normal Mode dialog windows indicating how many deferrals the user has remaining. Omit this key if you don't want the extra information.
Notification Icon -- This is the icon included on the right side of the Dialog Notification. Can be an app or a file path. Maps to SwiftDialog option: --icon

Notification Icon Dark Mode -- This is the icon included on the right side of the Dialog Notification. Can be an app or a file path. Use this key if you have to differentiate between light and dark mode icons. Maps to SwiftDialog option: --icon

Message Icon Dark Mode -- The icon used in your Normal and Aggressive Mode dialogs.
Banner Image -- Use this key to designate a file path to a Banner Image for your Normal and Aggressive Mode dialog windows. Maps to SwiftDialog option: --bannerimage

Banner Image Dark Mode -- Use this key to designate a file path to a Banner Image for your Normal and Aggressive Mode dialog windows. Use this key if you have to differentiate between light and dark mode banners. Maps to SwiftDialog option: --bannerimage
Additional Dialog Options -- Use this key to pass additional options you want for all dialog events. See SwiftDialog documentation for advanced options.
Additional Aggressive Mode Options -- Use this key to pass additional options you want for only Aggressive Mode dialog events. See SwiftDialog documentation for advanced options.
Additional Normal Options -- Use this key to pass additional options you want for only Normal Mode dialog events. See SwiftDialog documentation for advanced options.
Additional Notification Options -- Use this key to pass additional options you want for only Notification Mode dialog events. See SwiftDialog documentation for advanced options.
Applications to Ignore -- The applications which Renew ignores when checking for display assertions. (You can specify one or more, EX: zoom.us firefox).
Applications

Automatic Update Install Prompt -- Controls the automatic update install prompt. When enabled, presents users with the option to allow automatic download and install of available updates. If disabled, disallows automatic updates and requires manual installation every time.
Enable Automatic Silent Updates -- Controls automatic silent updates. If enabled, users will not be informed about updates and updates will be silently installed when the app quits.
Accept EndNote X9 EULA -- Set to 1 to accept EndNote X9 EULA and hide the dialog from users.
Show Getting Started -- Set to 0 to disable EndNote Getting Started prompts.
Suppress "Important Update" Messages -- Suppress "Important Update" messaging at first run. Correct value is the whole version number, e.g. 2019.7.24.0. Mulitple versions can be specified.
Client Environment -- Configures the client to run in either commercial mode or government compliance mode (GovSlack).
Hardware Acceleration -- Enable or disable hardware accelerated rendering via GPU.
Download Path -- Defines the download location for documents from Slack. This must be a valid user accessible path.
Default Team / Workspace -- Sets the default team/workspace for Slack sign-ins.
Release Channel -- Configure the client to receive updates from either the production or beta channel.
Auto Update -- Enable or disable auto updates.

Hide Password Expiration
