Password Expiration Custom Alert
Password Expiration Custom Warning Time -- Number of days remaining before the custom alert is shown, and in yellow.
Password Expiration Custom Alert Time -- Number of days remaining before the custom alert is shown, and in red.
Unannounced Password Changes Alert -- Alerts the user to Unannounced Password Changes, typically when the password was changed in AD and not from the user's system.
Unannounced Password Changes Message -- Message to be shown in an UPCAlert notification.
Unannounced Password Changes Action -- Path to a script or other binary to execute when a UPC Alert occurs.
Get Certificates Automatically -- Automatically request a certificate for a user when they don't have a valid certificate in the keychain.
Automatic Certificate Renewal -- Number of days until the certificate expires before automatically renewing it.
Exportable Private Key -- Allows the private key from any NoMAD generated certificate to be exported.
Automatic Certificate Cleaning -- Automatically remove extra certificates from the user's keychain. This will leave the 2 newest and the 2 oldest certificates.
Windows Certificate Authority -- FQDN of the Windows web CA for NoMAD to use for certificates.
Windows Certificate Authority Template -- Certificate template to request when using the Windows CA.
Wi-Fi Networks -- A list of wireless networks that the certificate created by NoMAD should be associated with.
Hide NoMAD Menubar Icon -- Removes the icon from the menu bar. Note that NoMAD still is in the menu bar, just with no icon and taking up less space.
Mount Shares with Finder -- Use the Finder instead of the API for automounted file shares.
Get Help Type -- Determines type of GetHelp function.
Get Help Options -- URL or Path for GetHelpType (<<serial>>, <<fullname>>, <<shortname>> and <<domain>> are currently supported as substitutions)
Self Service Path -- File path for a Self Service application not found automatically.
Hide 'About' Menu Item -- Hides the About menu item.
Hide 'Get Software' Menu Item -- Hides the Get Software menu item.
Hide 'Help' Menu Item -- Hides the Get Help menu item.
Show 'Home' Menu Item -- Shows the Home Directory share menu item.
Hide 'Lock Screen' Menu Item -- Hides the Lock Screen menu item.
Hide 'Preferences' Menu Item -- Disables the Preferences menu item.
Hide 'Quit' Menu Item -- Hides the Quit menu item.
Hide 'Renew Tickets' Menu Item -- Hides the Renew Tickets menu item.
Hide 'Sign Out' Menu Item -- Hides the Sign Out menu item.
Persist Password Expiration Countdown -- Shows the password expiration countdown even when the user is not logged into the domain.
Not Connected to Domain Message -- Message text to show in the menu bar when NoMAD is not connected to the AD domain.
Password Change Policy Message -- Message text to display in the password change dialog to help the user understand how complex they need to be.
Local Password Sync Message -- Message text for when a user is asked for their local password to sync their network password to their local account.
'About' Menu Item Text -- Menu item text for the About item.
'Change Password' Menu Item Text -- Menu item text for the Change Password item.
'File Servers' Menu Item Text -- Menu item text for the File Servers item.
'Get Certificate' Menu Item Text -- Menu item text for the Get Certificate item.
'Get Software' Menu Item Text -- Menu item text for the Get Software item.
'Get Help' Menu Item Text -- Menu item text for the Get Help item.
'Home Directory' Menu Item Text -- Menu item text for the Home Directory item.
'Renew Tickets' Menu Item Text -- Menu item text for the Renew Tickets item.
Username Menu Item Text -- Menu item text for the user name item before a user logs in.
Password Expiration Menu Item Text -- Menu item text for the password expiration item before a user logs in.
Carrie the Caribou Icons -- Changes the icon set to Carrie the Caribou.
NoMAD Connected Icon -- Path to a 16x16 pixel image to use as the icon in the menu bar when NoMAD is connected.
NoMAD Disconnected Icon -- Path to a 16x16 pixel image to use as the icon in the menu bar when NoMAD is not connected.
NoMAD Connected Dark Icon -- Path to a 16x16 pixel image to use as the icon in the menu bar when NoMAD is connected in dark mode.
NoMAD Disconnected Dark Icon -- Path to a 16x16 pixel image to use as the icon in the menu bar when NoMAD is not connected in dark mode.
Verbose Logging -- Enables verbose logging.
NoMAD Login Item -- Adds NoMAD to the user's start up items.
Post Sign In Command -- Path to a script or command to be run after a successful sign in.
Post Sign Out Command -- Path to a script or other binary to be run on sign out.
Network Change Action -- Path to a script that will be launched on network changes.
Auto Configuration Scheme -- Keyword to determine what auto configuration scheme to use.
Don't Show NoMAD Welcome Window -- Hides the Welcome window on first launch.
Don't Show Again Welcome Window Checkbox -- Shows the Welcome Screen, but checks the "Don't show again" box by default. Useful for when you want to show the Welcome screen only once.
Custom Welcome Window Path -- Path to a folder containing an index.html file and associated resources for displaying as a Welcome window.
Show Sign In Window on Launch -- Shows the Sign In window on launch.
Sign In Window Keychain -- Shows the Sign In window on launch unless the user has a password in the keychain.
Force Sign In Window on Top -- Makes the Sign In window the foremost window when a user is not signed in.
Force Sign In Window on Top Timer -- Time in seconds between the SignInWindowAlert making the Sign In window the foremost window.
Sign In Window Title -- Title of the Sign In window.
Sign In Window User Exclusions -- Local users that will not be shown the Sign In window automatically.
Network Subdomain -- A pre-configured Twingate network subdomain (eg. autoco from autoco.twingate.com). This avoids users needing to enter your Twingate network address on first run.
Start At Login -- Starts the Twingate Client upon user login
Suppress Data Privacy Screen -- Suppresses the first run Data Privacy screen
Suppress Education Screens -- Suppresses the first run Education screens
ADDomain -- The desired AD domain
Map Kerberos Principal Name -- The OIDC claim that has the kerberos principal name. This is used when logging in with OIDC and ADDomain is defined.

Should Update Kerberos User Principal ADDomain -- If the user principal has a domain name and the OpenID token does not match the ADDomain name, replace it with the ADDomain name. For example: bob@sub.example.com -> bob@example.com if ADDomain was example.com.
Client ID -- The OIDC client id public identifier for the app.
Client Secret -- Client Secret sometimes required by identity provider.
Create User as Admin -- When set to true and the user account is created, the user will be a local admin.
Skip User Setup Buddy -- When set to true and a new user home is created, the .skipbuddy file will be created at the top of the home folder to skip user setup screens.
Allow Users Claim -- The claim that contains the value to check for in the allowedUsersArray. Both must be defined.

Allowed Users -- List of users that are allowed to log in. An empty array or undefined array means any user can log in as long their cloud credentials are valid. The preference allowUsersClaim must be defined to a claim in the idToken that identifies the users.

Allow Login If Member Of Group -- (OIDC Only) List of groups whose members should be allowed to login. If the user is a member of any of these groups they can login regardless (including creating new local account) if authorization succeeds.

Create Admin If Group Member -- List of groups that should have members be given local administrator status. Local administrator status can be given on first authentication when account created, or on later sign in of existing user when a group member.
Claims To Add To Local User Account -- List of claims that should be added to the user local account. Will be prefixed with _xcreds_oidc_. Set as an Array of Strings of the claim.
System Info Additions -- Items to be added to the System Info Popover at login. Can be made dynamic by using the override script override to provide this setting

Should Switch To Login Window When Locked -- When set to true and the user locks the current session, XCreds will tell the system to switch to Login Window. The current session will stay active but the user will login with the XCreds Login Window to resume the session.
LocalFallback -- If the user attempts to login as an AD user and the login fails against AD, try against local user account if off domain or AD user not found.
Should Activate System Info Button -- Show the system info popover as active when first starting

Discovery URL -- The discovery URL provided by your OIDC / Cloud provider. For Google it is typically https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration and for Azure it is typically https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/.well-known/openid-configuration.
Enable Full Disk Encryption (FDE) -- Enabled FDE enabled at first login on APFS disks.
Save PRK -- Save the Personal Recovery Key (PRK) to disk for the MDM Escrow Service to collect.
FDE Recovery Key Path -- Specify a custom path for the recovery key.
Enable FDE Rekey -- Rotate the Personal Recovery Key (PRK).
Login Window Width -- Login Window webview width (Integer). If this is not defined, it will be full width. Minimum value of 150.
Login Window Height -- Login Window webview height (Integer). If this is not defined, it will be full height. Minimum value of 150.
LoadPage Title -- When no network connection or a profile is not defined, this title is shown in an HTML view to the user when cloud login is configured.

should Hide Login Window Logo -- Hide the login window logo.
Login Window Logo Path -- URL to an image to show icon in the username / password login window
Login Window Background Image URL -- URL to an image to show in the background while logging in. Default value: file:///System/Library/Desktop Pictures/Monterey Graphic.heic.
Login Window Background Image Alpha -- Alpha value of loginWindowBackgroundImage. Default value: 1

Login Window Secondary Monitors Background Image URL -- URL to an image to show in the background on secondary display while logging in. Default value: file:///System/Library/Desktop Pictures/Monterey Graphic.heic.
Menu Item Icon Data -- Base64 data of icon. Should be 48 x 48.
Menu Item Icon Checked Data -- Base64 data of icon with checkmark. Should be 48 x 48.
Menu Item Window BackgroundImageURL -- URL to an image to show in the background of the window that appears when logged in and prompting for Active Directory username and password.
Menu Item Background Image Alpha -- Alpha value of menuItemWindowBackgroundImageURL. Default value: 1
Login Window Background Image Fill Screen -- Set the background image to Fill Screen rather than Fit to Screen
Login Window Secondary Monitors Background Image Fill Screen -- Set the secondary monitor(s) background image to Fill Screen rather than Fit to Screen
Login Window Secondary Monitors Background Image Alpha -- Alpha value of loginWindowSecondaryMonitorsBackground. Default value: 1
Should Remove Menu Item Auto Launch -- When XCreds is installed, a launch agent is installed to automatically keep the menu item running when a user is logged in.
Should Use AD Native Password Change Menu Item -- When changing password via menu item, use the native UI to change password in Active Directory.

Password Change URL for Menu -- Add a menu item for changing the password that will open this URL when the menu item is selected. If shouldUseADNativePasswordChangeMenuItem is set to true, this value is not used.
Redirect URI -- The URI passed back to the webview after successful authentication. Default value: xcreds://auth/
Show Cloud Login By Default -- Determine if the Mac login window or the cloud login window is shown by default. When not set or set to true, show cloud login. If false, shows Mac login.
Password Change Check Rate Hours -- The number of hours between checks. Default value: 3. Minimum value: 0. Max value: 168.

Password Change Check Rate Minutes -- The number of minutes between checks. Default value: 0. Minimum value: 0. Max value: 59. This value is added to refreshRateHours. If refreshRateHours is 0, minimum for refreshRateMinutes becomes 5.
Scopes -- Scopes tell the identify provider what information to return. Note that the values are provided with a single space between them.
Request Google Refresh Token -- When using Google IdP, a refresh token may need be requested in a non-standard way.
Google Host Domain -- When using Google IdP, set the HD key to show the user's domain

Should Prompt For AD Password Change -- If the domain controller returns back that the password is expired or needs to be changed, prompt the user. If this is set to false, login will fail and an error message will be shown.
Show Sign In Menu Item -- Determine if the Sign In menu item is shown in the XCreds menu. When not set or set to true, show Sign In. If false, the Sign In menu item is hidden.
Should Suppress Local Password Prompt -- Do not prompt for local password.
Prefer Local Login over Cloud Login -- Favor using XCreds' local login screen over the cloud login UI.
Should Use Basic Auth With ROPG -- When using ROPG, do basic HTTP auth. Default: false
Use ROPG when logging in at login window -- When verifying password in the login window, use ROPG.
Use ROPG for menu login -- When verifying password in the menu app, use ROPG.

Should Use ROPG For Password Change Checking -- When verifying local password matches cloud password in the background, use ROPG. If set to false, the refresh token will be used to verify password change.

Should Use LDAP For Password Change Checking -- When verifying local password matches cloud password in the background, use Google LDAP. If set to false, the refresh token will be used to verify password change.
ROPG Resource -- Resource URL when using ROPG. Typically needed only for Azure. Common value is https://graph.microsoft.com

ROPG Response Value -- When a ROPG request is completed successfully to verify password, it may return an error that two factor is required. Add the string that is returned for the JSON response. For Azure, it is typically interaction_required.
Hide If Path Exists -- Don't show the UI if this key is defined and a file or folder exists at this path.

Alias Name -- Name of OIDC claim that contains an alias to add to a user account. Usually this is the "upn" (eg syd@twocanoes.com) so the user can log in at the standard login window the same as the IdP login window.
Automatically Refresh Login Window (seconds) -- Timer for automatically refreshing login screen in seconds. If set to 0, does not automatically refresh.
Cloud Login Text -- Text for return to cloud login on Mac login screen
Show About Menu -- Show the About Menu item menu. Default value: true

Skip FileVault Login -- Skip FileVault login during startup if FileVault is enabled. The current username and password are used to tell fdesetup to silently use the credentials during next reboot to unlock FileVault.

Skip FileVault Login as Admin -- Skip FileVault authentication at startup if FileVault is enabled. The admin credentials will be used to tell fdesetup to silently use the credentials during next reboot to unlock FileVault.

Should Show Menu Bar Sign In Without Login Window Sign In -- If the discovery URL is defined and there are no tokens or tickets, the sign in window in the user session will show even if the user did not log in from the XCreds Login Window

Show Configure WiFi -- Show Configure WiFi button in XCreds Login.
Show Shutdown Button -- Show Shutdown button in XCreds Login.
Show Restart Button -- Show Restart button in XCreds Login.
Show System Info Button -- Show Configure System Info in XCreds Login.
Show Preferences on Startup -- Show Settings on start if none are defined. Default value: false
Should Prompt for Migration -- Prompt for local account username and password if no account was mapped and there are standard users already on the system.
Should Allow Key Combo For Mac Login Window -- Allow key combo (control-option return) to switch logon window. Use command-option-control-return for Mac Login Window.
Key Code For Login Window Change -- key code for shouldAllowKeyComboForMacLoginWindow. If not defined, it is return or enter.
Show Mac Login Window button -- Show the Mac Login Window button in XCreds Login.
Show Local Only Checkbox -- Show the local only checkbox on the local login page
Username Placeholder Text -- Placeholder text in local / AD login window for username
Password Placeholder Text -- Placeholder text in local / AD login window for password
Show Support Status Message -- Show message in XCreds Login reminding people to buy support.
Show Quit Menu Item -- Show Quit in the menu item menu. Default value: true
Show Debug Message -- Show push notifications for authentication progress. Default value: false

Local Username -- When a user uses cloud login, XCreds will try and figure out the local username based on the email or other data returned for the IdP. Use this value to force the local username for any cloud login. Provide only the shortname.

Overwrite Password Silently -- Update the local user password silently to match the cloud / AD password. Requires access to admin credentials. See command line help to set admin username and password.
Hide Expiration -- Hide AD Expiration even if defined in AD Account
Local Admin User Name -- Username of local admin user. DO NOT SET THIS IN PREFERENCES. It is recommended to set this with the settingsOverrideScriptPath script.
Local Admin Password -- Password of local admin user. DO NOT SET THIS IN PREFERENCES. It is recommended to set this with the settingsOverrideScriptPath script.
Account Locked Password Dialog Title -- Title of dialog prompting user to enter in their prior local password when account is locked.

Should Skip Setting Secure Token For Admin -- Skip setting a secure token for the local admin user specified in XCreds. The token will be attempted if the local admin does not already have a secure token and a boot strap token is available.
Should Hide SecureToken Status -- Hide the status of SecureToken users in the popover status view

System Info Button Title -- The title of the button for system info in the bottom right corner of the login screen. This can either be plain text or one of these special values: .os, .hostname, .ipaddress, .serial, .mac, .computername, .ssid.

Verify Cloud Password -- When cloud password is changed and the local keychain password and local user account needs to be changed, a verification dialog can be shown to verify the password. Default value: true
Should Detect Network To Determine Login Window -- Check if network is up. If not, select username and password login window.
IDP Host Name -- Hostname of the page that has the password field. When the user submits the form, XCreds will use idpHostName to identify a page it needs to look for the password field.
IDP Host Names -- array of hostnames of the page that has the password field.
Additional AD Domains -- array of additional AD domains to accept
CCID Slot Name -- Name of slot for CCID reader for reading RFID cards
Should Allow Login Card Setup -- If an unknown RFID card is tapped, show option to pair with local account.
AD User Attributes To Add To Local User Account -- array of AD user attributes to add to local directory user account

Password Element ID -- Password element id of the html element that has the password. It is read by using JavaScript to get the value (for example, for Azure, the JavaScript document.getElementById('i0118').value is sent.

First Name OIDC Mapping/AD Attribute -- Local DS to OIDC/AD Mapping for First Name. Default value: "given_name" (OIDC), "givenName" (AD). map_firstname should be set to an OIDC claim/AD Attribute for first name.
Last Name OIDC Mapping -- Local DS to OIDC/AD Mapping for Last Name. Default value: "family_name" (OIDC), "sn" (AD). map_lastname should be set to an OIDC claim for last name.

Full Name OIDC Mapping/AD Attribute -- Local DS to OIDC/AD Attribute Mapping for Full Name. Default value: "name"(OIDC), "displayName" (AD). map_fullname should be set to an OIDC claim/AD Attribute for full name.

Username OIDC Mapping/AD Attribute -- Local DS to OIDC Mapping/AD Attribute for Name. Default value: "name" (OIDC), "userPrincipalName" (AD). map_username should be set to an OIDC claim/AD Attribute for name.

Full Username OIDC Mapping/AD Attribute -- Local DS to OIDC Mapping for Full Username (for example, freddy@twocanoes.com) Default value: "unique_name". map_username should be set to an OIDC claim for full username.
Map UID -- Local DS to OIDC Mapping/AD Attribute for UID at initial user creation. If not set, the uid will be set to the next available. If the mapped UID is used, login will fail.
Primary Group ID -- Primary Group ID when creating a new user. Default value 20.

Map OIDC claim to Password Expiry in Seconds -- Password expiry mapping to claim. If this value is set to an OIDC claim, the value in that claim should be the number of seconds from the token issued time (iat) to the expiry date.

Override Script Path -- Script to override defaults. Must return valid property list with specified defaults. Script must exist at path, be owned by _securityagent and writable and executable only by _securityagent.

UPN Suffix To Domain Mappings -- In some Active Directory environments, users do not use username@domain to login; they use a UPN suffix to make the username easier to use. This setting maps the UPN suffix to the correct AD domain name.

Title Font Size -- The font size of the title text shown in the top left of the AppBar window. Accepts numerical values between 16 and 32. Values outside this range will default to 22

Custom Logo -- The logo shown to the left of the title text. Can be a file path, URL to an image, or an SFSymbol name. Defaults to the 'Custom Logo (Dark Mode)' option if specified, or the 'app.badge.fill' SFSymbol if neither Custom Logo options are specified

Accent Colour -- Custom colour to be used for buttons and highlighting. Accepts hex colour codes (e.g., #0000FF). Defaults to macOS system accent colour if not specified

Installs Tab Enabled -- Determines whether the installs tab is enabled. Disabled by default. When disabled, users will see a message indicating installs are not allowed. When enabled, users can use the installs tab to install approved apps.

Allow Install Notifications -- Shows a macOS notification when installs complete. Requires a notifications configuration profile which approves com.zappl.AppBar notifications

entries.name: corp.sap.privileges
entries.title: SAP Privileges
entries.description: Use this section to define settings for the SAP Privileges app

keys.description: Expiration Interval -- Set a fixed time interval after which administrator privileges expire and revert to standard user rights
Expiration Interval Max -- Set a maximum time interval for a user to request administrative privileges

Allow Privilege Renewal -- Specifies whether expiring administrator privileges can be renewed. When set to true, the user receives a notification one minute before administrator privileges expire and can renew them.
Renewal Follows Auth Setting -- When set to true, renewing privileges requires the same kind of authentication as initially requesting administrator privileges (for example, Touch ID or password).
Allow CLI Biometric Authenication -- Specifies whether to allow biometric authentication in the PrivilegesCLI to obtain administrator privileges

Post Change Executable Path -- If set, the PrivilegesAgent executes the given application or script and provides the current user's user name ($1) and its privileges (admin or user, $2) as launch arguments

Post Change Action On Grant Only -- If set to true, the application or script, specified in PostChangeExecutablePath, will only be executed if administrator privileges are granted to a user, but not the privileges are revoked.

Pass Reason To Executable -- Specifies whether the reason that the user entered when requesting administrator privileges should be passed to the executable configured with the PostChangeExecutablePath key. The reason is passed as the third launch argument ($3).
Revoke Privileges at Login -- If set to true, the user's administrator privileges are revoked at login

Revoke At Login Excluded Users -- If RevokePrivilegesAtLogin is set to true, the specified users are excluded from privilege revocation at login. Provide an array of strings containing the short names of the users.

subkeys.description: User Short Name -- The short name of a user to exclude from privilege revocation at login.

keys.description: Hide Other Windows -- By default, Privileges hides open windows to show the desktop and ensure that only the Privileges window is visible on the screen
Enforce Privileges -- Enforces certain privileges. Whenever Privileges.app or the PrivilegesCLI command line tool are launched, the corresponding privileges are set.

Dock Toggle Timeout -- Sets a fixed timeout for the Dock tile's Toggle Privileges command. After this time, the admin rights are removed and set back to standard user rights. A value of 0 disables the timeout and allows the user to permanently toggle privileges.

Dock Toggle Max Timeout -- Set a maximum timeout for the Dock tile's Toggle Privileges command. This generally works the same way as the DockToggleTimeout but allows the user to choose every timeout value up to the one specified.
Limit to Group -- Limits the usage of Privileges.app to the given user group.
Limit to User -- Limits the usage of Privileges.app to the given user account.
Reason Required -- If ReasonRequired is set to true, the user must provide a reason for needing admin rights.
Reason Maximum Length -- Specifies the maximum number of characters the user can enter as the reason for becoming an admin
Reason Minimum Length -- Specifies the minimum number of characters the user has to enter as the reason for becoming an admin.
Reason Preset List -- If ReasonRequired is set to true, this key allows to pre-define a list of possible reasons (for becoming an admin) the user can choose from

subkeys.description: Localization -- Localization (de)
Localization -- Localization (en)
Localization -- Localization (es)
Localization -- Localization (it)
Unlocalized -- Unlocalization

keys.description: Reason Checking -- If set to true, the text the user enters for a reason is roughly parsed for valid words
Hide Settings Button -- If set to true, the Settings button is no longer displayed in the app
Hide Help Button -- If set to true, the Help (?) button is no longer displayed in the app.
Help Button Custom URL -- If specified, this URL is opened instead of the Privileges GitHub URL when the user clicks the help button. Must use http:// or https://.
Hide Settings From Dock Menu -- If set to true, the Settings menu item is no longer displayed in the Dock tile's menu
Hide Settings From Menu Bar -- If set to true, the Settings menu item is no longer displayed in the status item's menu.
Show in Menu Bar -- If set to true, a Privileges status item is displayed in the Menu Bar.
Require User Authentication -- Requires authentication before using Privileges.app. If set to true, the logged-in user is prompted to authenticate via Touch ID or by entering their account password.
Remote Logging Settings -- Remote logging settings

subkeys.description: Server Type
Server Address -- This will usually be an IP address, unless the syslog server is set up to respond using a DNS hostname.
Webhook Custom Data -- A dictionary of custom data (such as machine name or serial number) that is added to the webhook's JSON payload as the custom_data field.
Syslog Options -- Syslog-specific options
Log Facility -- Configure syslog facility.
Log Severity -- Configure syslog severity.
Server Port -- The port of the logging server.
Maximum Message Size -- Specify the maximum size of the syslog message (header + event message). If the syslog message is larger than the specified maximum, the message will be truncated at the end.

keys.description: Suppress Welcome Screen -- Suppress "Welcome to The Unarchiver!" slide.
Managed network shares -- Array with managed network shares that are centrally deployed to users.

subkeys.description: Server and share -- The share URL, e.g. smb://fileserver.example.com/share. Note: %USERNAME% is replaced at runtime with the user's macOS login name.
Authentication type -- Authentication method: krb (Kerberos/SSO), pwd (username + password), or guest. Default: krb.
Username (Optional) -- Pre-defines a username for pwd-type shares. If omitted, the user is prompted.
Mount point name (Optional) -- Overrides the local directory name used as the mount point. Only relevant when the mount location is not /Volumes. Leave blank to use the share name (recommended).

Externally managed Kerberos tickets -- Set to true if Kerberos tickets for this share are managed externally (AD binding, Jamf Connect, Apple SSO Extension). NSM will mount the share without interfering with ticket management and will not prompt for a Kerberos profile.

Per-share Kerberos realm (Optional) -- Per-share Kerberos realm override. Used together with externalKerberosManagement to identify which external profile to assign. Defaults to the global kerberosRealm setting.

Automatically mount -- true (default): the share is mounted automatically at startup and on network changes. false: the share appears in the menu but is never mounted automatically - the user can mount it on demand.

keys.description: Kerberos Realm -- Kerberos/AD domain for user authentication (e.g. EXAMPLE.COM). When set, NSM manages Kerberos ticket acquisition and renewal automatically. Required for app-managed Kerberos SSO.
Kerberos Profile Display Name -- Friendly display name for the Kerberos authentication profile shown in the app's Settings. If not set, the realm name (e.g. EXAMPLE.COM) is used as-is.
Username Override -- Overrides the %USERNAME% variable used in share paths. Use this when the local macOS login name differs from the AD or network username.
Single User Mode -- If true, automatic Kerberos sign-in and ticket renewal only process the default account. If false, all configured accounts are processed.

Password Expiration Countdown Start Day -- Passive warning. Days before password expiry when a silent countdown item first appears in the menu bar. The user only sees it when they open the menu. Set to 0 to disable all password expiration features entirely.

Password Expiration Notification Start Day -- Active warning. Days before password expiry when an alert dialog is shown automatically, once per calendar day. Set this lower than ExpirationCountdownStartDay so the dialog only interrupts when expiry is genuinely imminent.

Password Change URL -- URL of a web-based password self-service portal (SSPR). If set, a Change Password button in the expiration dialog opens this URL in the default browser. If not set, the user can change their password directly within NSM (requires kerberosRealm).

Allow Password Change -- When true, a permanent Change Password... item is shown in the menu bar at all times, even before the expiry threshold is reached. It automatically transforms into the expiry countdown when the threshold is reached.

Enable Autostart -- When deployed as a locked MDM key, the value is enforced on every app launch. When deployed as an unlocked default, it is applied once on the first launch only - after that, the user retains control.

Can Change Autostart -- Controls only the autostart toggle in the app's Settings UI. Set to false to grey it out. Does not affect MDM enforcement. To enforce the autostart state on every launch, deploy autostart as a locked key instead.
Allow to Quit App -- When true, the user can quit the app via the menu bar. Set to false to remove the Quit item entirely.
Unmount Shares on Exit -- When true, all managed shares are automatically unmounted when the app quits.

Mount path -- Path where network shares are mounted. The default is a localized folder in the user's home directory (e.g. ~/Network Shares). It is strongly recommended to leave this empty and use the default - changing it can break Finder integration.
Use the new default mount location -- If true, shares are mounted under /Volumes by default instead of the legacy per-user location. Ignored if 'location' is set.

Use Localized Mount Folder Name -- If false, always uses the English folder name 'Networkshares' for the legacy default mount path instead of a name localized to the user's language. Only relevant when 'useNewDefaultLocation' is false.

Clean up obstructing files and directories -- When true, NSM removes files and empty directories from the mount location that would prevent a share from mounting. Read the documentation carefully before enabling - this modifies the user's file system.
Help URL -- URL to your organization's internal helpdesk or IT documentation. When set, an About Network Share Mounter item appears in the menu bar, opening this URL in the default browser.
Menu Item: Connect Shares -- Controls the "Mount shares" action. Set to hidden to remove the item completely, or disabled to grey it out without removing it. Leave unconfigured to show it normally.

Menu Item: Disconnect Shares -- Controls the "Unmount shares" action. Set to hidden to remove the item completely, or disabled to grey it out without removing it. Leave unconfigured to show it normally.

Menu Item: Show Shares Mount Directory -- Controls "Show mounted shares" (opens the mount folder in Finder). Set to hidden to remove the item completely, or disabled to grey it out without removing it. Leave unconfigured to show it normally.

Menu Item: Show Shares List -- Controls the individual share items listed in the menu. Set to hidden to remove them completely, or disabled to grey them out without removing them. Leave unconfigured to show them normally.
Menu Item: Settings -- Controls the "Preferences..." item. Set to hidden to remove the item completely, or disabled to grey it out without removing it. Leave unconfigured to show it normally.

Menu Item: Check for Updates -- Controls the "Check for Updates..." item. Set to hidden to remove the item completely, or disabled to grey it out without removing it. Leave unconfigured to show it normally.

Menu Item: About -- Controls the "About Network Share Mounter" item (only visible when helpURL is set). Set to hidden to remove the item completely, or disabled to grey it out without removing it. Leave unconfigured to show it normally.
Menu Item: Quit -- Controls the "Quit Network Share Mounter" item. Set to hidden to remove the item completely, or disabled to grey it out without removing it. Leave unconfigured to show it normally.
Disable Auto Update Framework -- Master switch. Set to true to completely disable the Sparkle update framework. When disabled, no update checks occur and the Check for Updates menu item is removed.

Enable Automatic Update Checks -- When the framework is enabled, controls whether NSM actively checks for new versions in the background. Set to false to suppress checks while keeping the framework loaded.
Automatically Install Updates -- When true, updates are downloaded and installed automatically without asking the user for confirmation. Only takes effect when SUEnableAutomaticChecks is also true.
Send Diagnostic Data -- If true, diagnostic and crash data is sent to help improve the app. Independent of 'disableDiagnostics', which only hides the section in Settings.

Disable Diagnostics -- When true, hides the hidden "Diagnostics" trigger in Settings and General (five consecutive clicks) that lets users send NSM's unified-log activity to the developers for troubleshooting.
Enable AutoUpdater Framework -- Deprecated since version 4. Use 'disableAutoUpdateFramework' instead (inverted logic: enableAutoUpdater = true equals disableAutoUpdateFramework = false).
Network shares (deprecated, legacy) -- Legacy array with all network shares. Example: smb://filer.your.domain/share. Note: %USERNAME% will be replaced with the login name of the current user.

Connect on start -- Try to connect to Firezone using the saved token and configuration when the client application starts. If the authentication token is expired, the client will start in a disconnected state.

Start on login -- Start the Firezone client when the user logs into the machine. Requires the Firezone client to be running to take effect. In many cases you probably want to configure this using a Managed Login Items payload instead to force the client to be running.
Disable update check -- Disables the update check and notification for the Standalone variant of the macOS client. App Store variant versions 1.4.15 and higher already have this disabled.

URL -- The base URL to the folder containing the images.txt file or JSON information. Do NOT include trailing backslash.

Group Label -- String to be added after the baseURL. Using images.txt this adds after the baseURL and before images.txt.

Image Rotation Time -- Time each image will stay on screen.

entries.name: io.tailscale.ipn.macos
entries.title: Tailscale (MAS)
entries.description: Configure settings for the Mac App Store variant of the Tailscale client.

keys.description: Organization Details: Name -- Specifies the name of the organization managing Tailscale, for instance “XYZ Corp, Inc.”. The value will be displayed in the Tailscale client, so that users can easily reach your internal support resources.

Organization Details: Caption -- Specifies a caption to be displayed in the Managed By view in the Tailscale client. Use this string value to provide your users with information on how to reach support resources for Tailscale in your organization.

Organization Details: Support URL -- Specifies a URL pointing to a help desk webpage, or other helpful resources for users in the organization. Clicking the Support button in the Tailscale UI will open this webpage.

Automatically start Tailscale when the user logs in -- The first time the application is opened on a Mac, Tailscale installs a macOS login helper. This allows Tailscale to start automatically when the user logs into their account.
Keep Tailscale always connected -- Prevents users from disconnecting from the tailnet or exiting the client.
Require a reason for disconnection -- Requires users to submit a reason when disconnecting the Tailscale client. User-provided reasons display in the Configuration logs page of the admin console.

Reconnection timer -- Sets how long the client can remain disconnected from the tailnet before automatically reconnecting. Use a Go-style duration string, for example 24h or 5h25m30s. An empty string or a zero duration disables automatic reconnection.

Force Tailscale to always be running -- When set to true, this boolean instructs Tailscale to always be connected and actively monitor the tunnel state for disconnections. The Disconnect toggle will be disabled, to prevent users from disabling the VPN themselves.

Suppress DHCP Option 121 warnings -- By default, Tailscale v1.68 and later detect when DHCP Option 121 is being used, and the client will display a warning to the user in the UI when usage of this option is detected.
Suggested or required tailnet name -- Specifies one or more tailnets to suggest or require during device registration.

Custom control server URL -- The LoginURL policy can be used to specify a custom control server URL. This should not be changed unless you are not using the standard Tailscale server. Use this policy if you’re deploying your own server, such as Headscale.
Auth key -- Specifies an auth key used to authenticate managed devices without user interaction. Clients automatically try to use the auth key when launched unless already logged in.

Custom browser for authentication -- Controls the browser used to open authentication URLs. Set this to the bundle identifier of the preferred browser. If the specified bundle is not present, the user's default system browser is used.
Forced Exit Node ID -- Forces the Tailscale client to always use the given exit node. This can be useful if you wish to route all Internet traffic through a node for inspection or logging purposes.

Allow a different exit node when forced -- Lets users select a different exit node when ExitNodeID is set to auto:any, which requires the use of an exit node. It does not allow disabling exit node usage entirely.

Allowed suggested exit nodes -- Controls which exit nodes are recommended in the Tailscale client and through tailscale exit-node suggest. When ExitNodeID is set to auto:any, this list specifies the allowed regionally-routed exit nodes. If unset, all exit nodes are allowed.

subkeys.description: Exit Node ID -- The ID of an exit node device. You can find device IDs on the Machines page of the admin console or by using the Tailscale API.

keys.description: Advertise as exit node -- Controls whether the device advertises itself as an exit node for use by other users and their devices.

Key Expiration Notice Interval -- The KeyExpirationNotice policy controls how long before key expiry should a notice be displayed. The default is 24 hours ("24h"). Use a Go-style Duration for this policy value, for instance "24h" or "5h25m30s".
Allow Local Network Access when an exit node is in use -- Allow Local Network Access determines whether users can still access devices on the local network while using an exit node.
Use Tailscale Subnets -- Determines whether the client accepts subnets advertised by other nodes in your tailnet.
Set whether device hostnames can be modified -- The Hostname policy allows IT administrators to override the hostname configured in the operating system and reported to the coordination server.
Use Tailscale DNS Settings -- Determines whether to apply the DNS configuration provided by the coordination server when the tunnel is connected.
Allow incoming connections -- Determines whether Tailscale should allow incoming connections to the device.
Gather device posture data -- Enables gathering of device posture data.
Show/hide exit nodes picker -- Shows or hides all UI items to choose an exit node in the Tailscale client.
Show/hide tailnet lock settings -- Shows or hides the "Manage Tailnet lock" menu item.
Show/hide the "Reset to Defaults" menu item -- Shows or hides the "Reset to Defaults" menu item.
Show/hide "Run as Exit Node" menu item -- Shows or hides the "Run as Exit Node" menu item, controlling the user's ability to toggle this option.
Show/hide "Start on Login" menu item -- Shows or hides the "Start on Login" menu item, controlling the user's ability to toggle this option.

Show/hide Debug menu -- Shows or hides the debug menu in the Tailscale client. On macOS, this system policy will also hide any information displayed when holding down the Option key while clicking on the Tailscale menubar item.
Show/hide "Update Available" menu item -- Shows or hides the "Update Available" menu item which appears when a newer version of Tailscale is available.

Hide categories of network devices -- Can be used to hide one or more categories of network devices normally displayed in the Tailscale client. Administrators can choose to hide: devices owned by the current user; devices owned by other users; tagged devices.

allowedValueTitles: Devices belonging to the current user

keys.description: Suppress IP Address Copied notifications -- When you use the Tailscale menu bar item to copy to the Clipboard the IP address of a device, a notification displaying the IP address is presented. Use this to suppress this Copied IP address to clipboard notification.
Suppress the app window intro flow -- Set to true to suppress the "Welcome to the Tailscale app" modal window introduction that appears when you log in to Tailscale on a device for the first time.

Hide the macOS dock icon after all windows close -- The Tailscale dock icon on macOS appears whenever an application window exists. By default, Tailscale leaves an icon in the dock to support quickly reopening the main application window. Set this to true to hide the dock icon after all windows close.
Hide the CLI integration installer -- When set to hide, the user will not be able to install the CLI helper, and will instead be told to contact their administrator.

Show/hide the first launch onboarding flow -- Shows or hides the client onboarding flow that appears the first time Tailscale starts on a device. Hide it if end-users are already familiar with the product. On macOS, typically deploy a VPN configuration profile when hiding the onboarding flow.

Suppress the first launch onboarding flow -- When you start Tailscale on your Mac for the first time, an onboarding flow is presented. It explains the Tailscale privacy policy, and guides the user in setting up the VPN configuration on their Mac.
Hide the VPN On Demand menu item -- The VPNOnDemandSettings policy can be used to show or hide the VPN On Demand menu item.

VPN On Demand is user-configured -- Instructs Tailscale not to modify the VPN On Demand configuration, so that MDM-deployed OnDemandRules remain in effect. Deploy this together with VPNOnDemandSettings set to hide when providing your own VPN On Demand rules.

Hide the macOS dock icon after all windows close -- The Tailscale dock icon on macOS appears whenever an application window exists. By default, Tailscale leaves an icon in the dock to support quickly reopening the main application window. Set this to true to hide the dock icon after all windows close.
Hide the CLI integration installer -- When set to hide, the user will not be able to install the CLI helper, and will instead be told to contact their administrator.

Show/hide the first launch onboarding flow -- Shows or hides the client onboarding flow that appears the first time Tailscale starts on a device. Hide it if end-users are already familiar with the product. On macOS, typically deploy a VPN configuration profile when hiding the onboarding flow.

Suppress the first launch onboarding flow -- When you start Tailscale on your Mac for the first time, an onboarding flow is presented. It explains the Tailscale privacy policy, and guides the user in setting up the VPN configuration on their Mac.
Hide the VPN On Demand menu item -- The VPNOnDemandSettings policy can be used to show or hide the VPN On Demand menu item.

VPN On Demand is user-configured -- Instructs Tailscale not to modify the VPN On Demand configuration, so that MDM-deployed OnDemandRules remain in effect. Deploy this together with VPNOnDemandSettings set to hide when providing your own VPN On Demand rules.
Base URL for Munki repository.
Client Identifier -- Identifier for Munki client. Usually is the same as a manifest name on the Munki server.
Managed Install Directory -- Folder where Munki keeps its data on the client.
Local Only Manifest -- Defines the name of your LocalOnlyManifest. Setting this activates the feature. Unsetting it means Munki will remove the file on the next run.
Suppress Auto Install -- Munki will not automatically install or remove items.
Suppress Loginwindow Install -- Munki will not install items while idle at the loginwindow except for those marked for unattended_install or unattended_uninstall.

Install Apple Software Updates -- Install updates from an Apple Software Update server, in addition to "regular" Munki updates. Prior to Munki 7, this controlled whether Munki would notify about AND install Apple updates.

Install Apple Software Updates Only -- Only install updates from an Apple Software Update server. No Munki repository is needed or used. No longer really useful in Munki 7+, since Munki 7 only notifies about Apple updates rather than installing them.
Include Major OS Updates in Apple Software Updates -- If true (and InstallAppleSoftwareUpdates is also true), include major OS updates when displaying/notifying about available Apple updates.

Unattended Apple Updates -- Updates that declare no "must-close" applications, or have one or more "must-close" applications, none of which is running, and do not require a logout or restart will be installed as part of a normal periodic background run without notifying the…
Perform FileVault Authorized Restarts -- Munki will attempt to perform a filevault auth restart.
FileVault Credentials Path -- Absolute path to a plist file containing filevault credentials in key/value format. Used to perform auth restarts.
Emulate Profile Support (Big Sur) -- A bit of hack and not supported by Apple, it is disabled by default.
Suppress Update Notifications -- Managed Software Center will never notify the user of available updates. Managed Software Center can still be manually invoked to discover and install updates.
Suppress Stop Button On Install -- Managed Software Center will hide the stop button while installing or removing software, preventing users from interrupting the install.
Require Logout for Installs & Uninstalls -- Managed Software Center will require a logout for all installs or removals.
Show Removal Detail -- Managed Software Center will display detail for scheduled removals.
Show Optional Installs For Higher OS Versions -- Managed Software Center.app will show optional installs and updates that apply to macOS versions higher than the currently installed version.

Days Between Notifications -- Number of days between user notifications from Managed Software Center. Set to 0 to have Managed Software Center notify every time a background check runs if there are available updates.
Use Notification Center Days -- Number of days Notification Center notifications should be used before switching to launching Managed Software Center.

Offer To Quit Blocking Apps -- If true, if there are any running blocking_applications for pending updates, a sheet will be displayed allowing the user to direct Managed Software Center to attempt to quit the blocking applications.
Offer To Force Quit Blocking Apps -- If this (and MSCOfferToQuitBlockingApps) is true, if a "polite" attempt to quit an application fails, a button to force quit the application will be displayed.

Offer To Update Others -- If there is a mix of pending updates, some of which are blocked by open applications, and some that are not, and this preference is true (and so is MSCOfferToQuitBlockingApps), a button will be shown to allow users to proceed with updating the…

Package Verification Mode -- Controls how Munki verifies the integrity of downloaded packages. (none = No integrity check is performed, hash = Integrity check is performed if package info contains checksum information, hash_strict = Integrity check is performed, and fails if…
Allowed Notification Window -- If true, users can open the Managed Software Center settings window to specify allowed time windows for notifications.
Allowed Notification Window Start -- The earliest hour that can be selected for allowed notifications.
Allowed Notification Window End -- Only hours earlier than this can be selected (non-inclusive).
Follow HTTP Redirects -- Defines whether Munki will follow all, some or no redirects from the web server. (none = The default behaviour.
Additional HTTP Headers -- This key provides the ability to specify custom HTTP headers to be sent with all curl() HTTP requests.

subkeys.description: HTTPHeader -- An HTTP header in "Header: Value" format.

keys.description: Ignore System Proxies -- HTTP and/or HTTPS proxies set system-wide will be ignored, connections will be made directly.
Download Retries -- Number of times to retry a failed download. Valid values are 0-10. Set to 0 to disable retries.
Download Retry Sleep Seconds -- How many seconds to wait between download retries. Valid values are 1-30.
Base Package URL -- Base URL for Munki pkgs. Useful if your packages are served from a different server than your catalogs or manifests.
Base Catalog URL -- Base URL for Munki catalogs. Useful if your catalogs are served from a different server than your packages or manifests.
Base Manifest URL -- Base URL for Munki manifests. Useful if your manifests are served from a different server than your catalogs or manifests.
Base Icon URL -- Base URL for product icons. Useful if your icons are served from a different server or different directory than the default.
Base Client Resource URL -- Base URL for custom client resources for Managed Software Center. Useful if your resources are served from a different server or different directory than the default.
Client Resources Filename -- Specific filename to use when requesting custom client resources.
Help URL -- URL to open/display when the user selects "Managed Software Center Help" from Managed Software Center's Help menu.

License Info URL -- URL for Munki to query a webserver to determine if there are available seats for licensed software (or any software you wish to make available via optional_installs, yet control the number of deployed copies).

Software Update Server URL -- Catalog URL for Apple Software Updates. If undefined or empty, Munki will use the same catalog that the OS uses when you run Apple's Software Update application or call /usr/sbin/softwareupdate.
Use Client Certificate -- Use an SSL client certificate when communicating with the Munki server. Requires an https:// URL for the Munki repo.
Client Certificate Acceptable CAs -- Acceptable client certificate issuing CA distinguished names. Meant to be used when a server does not advertise CA names.

keys.description: Use Client Certificate CN As Client Identifier -- Use the CN of the client certificate as the Client Identifier. Used in combination with the UseClientCertificate key.
Client Certificate Path -- Absolute path to a client certificate. There are 3 defaults for this key. Concatenated cert/key PEM file accepted.
Client Key Path -- Absolute path to a client private key.
Software Repo CA Path -- Path to the directory that stores your CA certificate(s). See the curl man page for more details on this parameter.
Software Repo CA Certificate -- Absolute path to your CA Certificate.
Log File -- Primary log is written to this file. Other logs are written into the same directory as this file.
Log to Syslog -- Log to syslog in addition to ManagedSoftwareUpdate.log.
Logging Level -- Higher values cause more detail to be written to the primary log.
Log Enabled -- Log user actions in the GUI.
Debug Log Enabled -- Debug logging for Managed Software Center.

Access Key -- Munki has a feature which enables Mac administrators to use middleware to change munki's HTTP request. S3-Auth uses this feature to create the HTTP headers necessary to authenticate to S3. AccessKey for S3 bucket.

Munki has a feature which enables Mac administrators to use middleware to change munki's HTTP request. S3-Auth uses this feature to create the HTTP headers necessary to authenticate to S3. Region for S3 bucket.

Secret Key -- Munki has a feature which enables Mac administrators to use middleware to change munki's HTTP request. S3-Auth uses this feature to create the HTTP headers necessary to authenticate to S3. SecretKey for S3 bucket.

S3 Endpoint -- Munki has a feature which enables Mac administrators to use middleware to change munki's HTTP request. S3-Auth uses this feature to create the HTTP headers necessary to authenticate to S3. S3 Endpoint for bucket.
Ignore Middleware -- If true, Munki will ignore installed middleware. Useful for when moving away from middleware.

Aggressive Update Notification Days -- This preference controls how many days after one or more pending updates are ignored that aggressive user notification begins. Setting this to 0 never triggers this aggressive behavior.

Custom Sidebar Items -- Custom sidebar configuration for Managed Software Center, overriding the default Software/Categories/My Items/Updates sidebar. Each array item is a dict with 'title', 'icon' (an SF Symbol name), and 'page' (a munki:// URL) key.

Lab Mode -- Lab Mode eases the deployment of Particulars in a computer lab or other mass deployment. See the documentation for more information.
Show Particulars on the Desktop -- The default mode of Particulars is to present system information on the desktop. This can be disabled, usually in favor of showing Particulars in the menu bar.

Show Particulars in the Menu Bar -- Adds an item to the macOS menu bar that allows quick access to system information. Secondary-clicking on the menu bar item shows a menu with settings, copying, and other functions.
Detail Level -- Adjust detail level options. See documentation URL for instructions.

Preferred Display -- Sets the display (or monitor) on which Particulars will show desktop system information. If the display is later unavailable, Particulars will default back to the primary display. The value is an integer, taking 2 for the 2nd display, for example.
Desktop Position -- Sets the relative position of desktop system information.
Desktop Margin -- When displaying system information on the desktop, Particulars uses all available screen size, inset by a default margin of 21pt. Margins can be adjusted.
Desktop Top Margin -- Overrides desktopMargin for the top desktop margin
Desktop Bottom Margin -- Overrides desktopMargin for the bottom desktop margin
Desktop Left Margin -- Overrides desktopMargin for the left desktop margin
Desktop Right Margin -- Overrides desktopMargin for the right desktop margin
Text Theme -- Sets the theme of desktop system information. Each theme has a corresponding number.

Light or Dark Text -- Particulars has 3 options for the shade of the desktop system information: automatic, light text, or dark text. The automatic setting scans the current desktop picture to determine what setting to use.
Text Size -- Sets the preferred text size for the desktop system information in points. The default is 18. Values between 12 and 24 are typical. (Value may be scaled down to fit.)
Drop Shadow -- Determines whether the desktop system information has a drop shadow behind it.
Label Case -- Sets the letter case of the labels. Each case option has a corresponding number.
Menu Bar Widget Appearance -- Sets the appearance of the menu bar widget.
Menu Bar Widget Text Size -- Sets the preferred text size in the menu bar widget in points. The default is 12. Values below 9 and above 24 are ignored. (Value may be scaled down to fit.)
Detachable Menu Bar Widget -- Allows the menu bar widget to be drug away from the menu bar and appear in a floating window.
Menu Bar Icon -- Specifies an alternative menu bar icon. Valid values are: classic, quatrefoil, quatrefoil.fill, and any valid SF Symbol.

Show All Active Network Interfaces -- When enabled in the detail level, Particulars displays information about the primary active network interface. This setting expands that to include information about all active network interfaces.
Show DHCP Lease Time Remaining -- In the default network information, Particulars shows the DHCP server address and the length of the DHCP lease. This setting adds the remaining lease time.
MAC Address Format -- By default, MAC (Media Access Control) addresses are formatted with colon separators and in lowercase. Use this setting to select another MAC address format.

Network Detail Level -- By default, all network information is displayed except the Wi-Fi SSID. It is possible to construct a custom set of network information. Use this preference to create a custom network detail level. See documentation URL for instructions.

Network Notifications -- When enabled, Particulars will post system notifications when it detects a change in the primary IPv4 address or the public IP address. Notifications are also governed by settings in the Notifications pane of System Settings.
Use CIDR Notation for Subnet Mask -- This setting displays subnet masks in the short CIDR (Classless Inter-domain Routing) notation. For example, 255.255.254.0 will show as /23.
Explicit No Networks Detected message -- Displays an error message if no active network interfaces are found (assuming network is enabled in 'detailLevel').
Checking for new version in the Mac App Store -- Particulars checks for new Particulars versions in the Mac App Store. This check can be disabled.
CPU Core Count -- Adds a count of CPU cores to the CPU particular. Changing this setting requires a restart of the application to take effect.
Date Format -- This modifies the format of the date and time for the Boot Time particular. Follows a Unicode standard https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr35/tr35-31/tr35-dates.html#Date_Format_Patterns
Disable Crash Manager -- Organizations can disable all reporting of crashes to the developer by setting this to true using Managed Preferences.
Disk Free Space Format -- Free/available disk space can be displayed in multiple ways. See documentation URL for options.
Show Disk Free Space for Non-Boot Volumes -- By default, Particulars only shows disk space for the boot disk. Enable this setting to show disk space for other disks.
Skip the First Run Experience -- On first run, Particulars displays a welcome window that describes how it runs on the desktop and then hides all other apps and opens the settings window.
Header -- Header text is displayed in a separate paragraph above all particulars. Any leading or trailing whitespace is removed when displayed.
Footer -- Footer text is displayed in a separate paragraph below all particulars. Any leading or trailing whitespace is removed when displayed.

Hide Dock Icon -- Enabling this setting removes Particulars from the macOS Dock. Changing this setting while Particulars is running will automatically restart Particulars and open the Settings window.

Ignore Hiding -- When Particulars is running with the Dock icon shown, it will be hidden along with all other apps when you select Hide Others from another application's menu. This preference allows you to keep Particulars visible.
Operating System Version Name -- This setting adds the operating system version's marketing name (e.g., Big Sur, Catalina, etc) to the Operating System particular.
Lab Mode -- Lab Mode eases deployment of Particulars in a computer lab or data center.
Detail Level -- Adjust detail level options. See documentation URL for instructions.
Label Case -- Sets the letter case of the labels. Each case option has a corresponding number.
Show DHCP Lease Time Remaining -- Particulars shows the DHCP server address and the length of the DHCP lease. Setting this preference will also show the remaining lease time.
MAC Address Format -- By default, MAC (Media Access Control) addresses are formatted with colon separators and in lowercase. Use this preference to select another MAC address format.

Network Detail Level -- By default, all network information is displayed. It is possible to construct a custom set of network information. Use this preference to create a custom network detail level. See documentation URL for instructions.
Subnet Mask CIDR Notation -- Use this preference to have Particulars display subnet masks in the short CIDR (Classless Inter-domain Routing) notation. For example, 255.255.254.0 will show as /23.
Show CPU Core Count -- Adds a count of CPU cores to the CPU item. Changing this preference requires a restart of the application/widget to take effect.
Show Disk Free Space -- Free/available disk space can be displayed in multiple ways. See documentation URL for options.

Enable Automatic Silent Updates -- Controls automatic silent updates. If enabled, users will not be informed about updates and updates will be silently installed when the app quits.
